stories.title: 76ers rule out Jaylen Brown (hamstring), list Joel Embiid (illness) as questionable for Friday's game vs. Pacers
stories.summary: Brown may have reinjured the hamstring that caused him to miss two games last week, and Embiid could miss his third consecutive game.
stories.detailText: The Philadelphia 76ers could be short-staffed when they take on the Indiana Pacers in NBA Cup play on Friday night. Shooting guard Jaylen Brown has already been ruled out with a hamstring injury. Center Joel Embiid is listed as questionable due to a lingering illness that has sidelined him for Philadelphia's last two games. Brown picked up the hamstring issue in Wednesday's NBA Cup win over the Miami Heat. He left the game late in the first half and did not return. The guard missed two games last week with a left hamstring strain, but returned to action against the Portland Trail Blazers and played 29 minutes. Toward the end of the first half, the Philadelphia guard reached toward his left hamstring and shook his head before checking himself out of the game. Embiid is dealing with an illness, though not much has been released about what symptoms he may be dealing with. Regardless, he has missed two consecutive games. The center was listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Heat, but was downgraded before the game. With no Embiid and no Brown for a half, LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey took over and led the 76ers to a win over the Heat on Wednesday. James logged his first triple-double as a 76er with 25 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists. Maxey added 30 points, 4 rebounds and 6 assists. The win moved Philadelphia to 15-4. Friday's game against Indiana is the front end of a back-to-back, and a win would help the 76ers clinch their NBA Cup group.

stories.title: Jaylen Brown out against Pacers; Joel Embiid (illness) questionable
stories.summary: The 76ers' Jaylen Brown (hamstring) is out for Friday's NBA Cup game against the Pacers. Joel Embiid (illness) is questionable.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown (left hamstring) will miss Friday night's NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers . Center Joel Embiid , who has missed the last two games with an illness, is questionable. After scoring his sixth point of Wednesday night's win over the Miami Heat on a step-back jump shot late in the second quarter, Brown immediately shook his head and grabbed his hamstring then signaled to the Sixers bench that he needed to check out of the game. The injury started for Brown in last week's win over the Brooklyn Nets in which he tied his season high of 31 points. Brown left that game early because of a left hamstring strain and missed the Sixers' next two wins over the Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks . He returned in Monday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers , scoring 20 points. After that game, Brown said he had "a little bit of soreness." For the season, Brown is averaging 21.4 points, six rebounds and 3.4 assists. Friday's game is the final of NBA Cup group play. With a win, the 76ers will clinch Eastern Conference Group B and advance to the knockout rounds for the first time.

stories.title: A Thanksgiving thank you to the community that changed my life
stories.summary: Happy Thanksgiving everyone! This community is truly a special place.
stories.detailText: Disclaimer ** While this article mentions Phoenix Suns experiences, this piece is about the gratitude that comes with covering the team . So if you’re looking for a piece analyzing the team’s hot streak or Jalen Green’s trade value, feel free to check out other content on Bright Side. ** Hey everyone! It is well known in sports media circles that SB Nation sites serve as an incubation lab for young journalists. Being able to write about professional sports, and maybe even get paid to do so, helps so many people achieve their dreams much earlier than they expected while gaining real-world experience in what it’s like to work in this profession full-time. From covering the Super Bowl, the NBA Draft, or Hall of Fame ceremonies, what you put into your time at SB Nation is what you get out of it. But to earn those opportunities, you need people to trust you. And on this 2026 Thanksgiving, I’d like to thank the Bright Side community for helping me land my first full-time job in sports media. First and foremost, thank you to every reader. Whether you’re a frequent post commenter or this is the first Bright Side piece you’ve ever read, I appreciate you. Knowing there are always people to serve and that we get to share the unique access we have at the NBA Draft, playoff games, Summer League, and many other events keeps our purpose strong: serving passionate Suns fans. To the late, great Dave King, Harrison Faigen, and John Voita, thank you for taking a chance on a 20-year-old and allowing me to fly out to Philadelphia to cover Kevin Durant and reigning MVP Joel Embiid. Your trust in me is what has allowed me to conduct one-on-one interviews with Khaman Maluach and Rasheer Fleming after they were drafted, sit down with Amar’e Stoudemire and Mike D’Antoni before their Hall of Fame inductions, and cover dozens of NBA events across the country. I’ve met so many of my media idols and learned so many lessons about the industry at a much younger age than I expected. This is the wordy DM I sent to John Voita when I was 19, looking for a chance. ANY chance to write about the NBA. The relationships, experiences, and lessons I’ve gained in the first few years of my media career helped me stay sane and confident during my job search. It took me about six months to find my first full-time job in sports media after graduating from Syracuse in May (where the voice of the Suns, Jon Bloom, also went!). While many people have had to wait much longer to find their first job, and plenty spend more than six months between gigs, the process still took a toll on me. But I knew that, thanks to my experience at Bright Side, I’d eventually end up somewhere doing what I love. So, on a day centered around thankfulness, thank you, Bright Side, for helping me land my first full-time job in sports media. I’m now working as an on-air host at WeTheHobby , where I broadcast, livestream, and podcast about the latest happenings in the NBA collectibles space. My Bright Side coverage is still the same as it’s been since I joined the staff, but now I get to do it knowing that I’m a full-time sports media professional and that what I’ve learned from being a part of this community has played a major role in getting me here. I’m truly grateful. Happy Thanksgiving, everyone! If only there were NBA games on today! Best, Holden Sherman

stories.title: The Jordan Clarkson moment that shows why Knicks’ unique bench works so well
stories.summary: It was a guy who didn’t play who served as a catalyst for the Knicks’ most all-around win this year.
stories.detailText: Jordan Clarkson; Pacome Dadiet It was a guy who didn’t play who served as a catalyst for the Knicks’ most all-around win this year. Coach Mike Brown used 12 players in the team’s 121-102 win over the Cavs on Wednesday night at Madison Square Garden. Without OG Anunoby (calf strain) and Miles McBride (adductor tightness), it meant end-of-the-bench reserves got a rare chance to see some action. Pacôme Dadiet had seven points in 14 minutes. Rookie Tyler Nickel, making his NBA debut (he has spent this year in the G League), got nine minutes and had five points. Mohamed Diawara got four minutes and chipped in three points. James Wiseman saw six minutes of action and helped seal the win with a few crucial rebounds late — he finished with six offensive rebounds. Under Brown’s anything-goes system, nobody is too far away from getting a chance. His love of experimentation, particularly early in the year, means players seemingly out of the rotation will get their opportunity to prove themselves at some point. Jordan Clarkson of the New York Knicks smiles before an NBA basketball game against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images It has cultivated an ego-less culture among the bench players, where they know the minutes will look different every night. It’s a system of basketball socialism of sorts. But it’s only possible because one member of that group set the tone for the rest. “As a coach, you could want to do that, but you have to have others around you that will at least support it initially to see how it turns out,” Brown said. “And a huge, huge, huge catalyst for that was Jordan Clarkson. Jordan Clarkson was the one, if you’re talking about giving 100 percent out there to what allows me to do that, I think Jordan Clarkson gave me at least 90 percent of the opportunity to do it, because here’s an accomplished veteran that could be in the rotation for almost any team out there, let alone a championship team, and I can literally play him six straight games and then sit him 10 straight games and he’s gonna be the same dude every fricken’ day. And he’s gonna talk the same way to his teammates. Not ‘can you believe what Mike Brown did?’ Nah, he’s gonna be the same dude, uplift the group, and then when I call his number again, he’s gonna be ready to go. “He’s a guy that, even when he gets done playing, it’s one of those things where you hope that he can just be a part of this organization in some way, shape or form until he doesn’t want to be part of this organization. He’s that type of person, in my opinion.” Clarkson missed Wednesday’s game — the fourth straight he’s been sidelined due to plantar fasciitis. But it was he who helped Dadiet — who has largely underwhelmed, now in his third year after the Knicks drafted him in the first round — deliver his best game as a pro. “JC is always big on that, telling guys to stay ready,” Jose Alvarado said. “He was in [Dadiet’s] ear the whole shootaround [Wednesday morning]. Just telling everybody to stay ready because you never know when your name is called.” New York Knicks forward Pacome Dadiet (4) puts up a shot against the Cleveland Cavaliers at Madison Square Garden in New York, Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. Jason Szenes for NY Post Alvarado himself had his best game of the year with 21 points in 19 minutes. But it wasn’t long ago that he was out of the rotation, with Tyler Kolek having usurped him as the backup point guard. But Brown has recently been experimenting with having Alvarado on the floor at the same time as Jalen Brunson, in order to allow Brunson to play off-the-ball more. And Brown has liked the results. That has meant Alvarado is now cutting back into Kolek’s minutes, despite Kolek continuing to play well. That could rub other players on other teams the wrong way –— losing minutes despite not doing anything wrong, simply because the coach wants to try something new and see how it works out. For the bench players, nothing is set in stone, regardless of how you play. This team embraces it, though. Brown compared the way this bench pulls for one another to the championship Spurs and Warriors teams he was an assistant on. It’s a rare luxury for a coach to have. “We care about each other,” Landry Shamet, currently the top dog of that bench unit, said. “We want to win for each other. We’re willing to take on different roles and we know that we’ve got each other’s back. If Jose’s got it going and my minutes are shortened, awesome. And vice versa. All of us, Deuce [McBride] included in that, I would throw him in that as well, all of us kind of feel that way. That’s really cool. “I’ve been saying it, I’ve been a broken record about it, but you don’t see that — that’s very rare where no ego or ulterior motives get involved. That’s something special that you want to be a part of.” Something special, sparked by a special personality in Clarkson.

stories.title: 76ers' Jaylen Brown exits with recurrence of hamstring issue
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown exited the 76ers' NBA Cup game against the Heat and was ruled out because of left hamstring tightness.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- 76ers forward Jaylen Brown exited Wednesday night's 111-104 NBA Cup win against the Heat and was ruled out because of left hamstring tightness. Coach Nick Nurse said postgame that Brown would undergo imaging and that the team would have an update on his hamstring Thursday. After scoring his sixth point of the night on a step-back jump shot late in the second quarter, Brown immediately shook his head and grabbed the hamstring then signaled to the Sixers bench that he needed to check out of the game. The injury started for Brown in last week's win over the Brooklyn Nets in which he tied his season high of 31 points. Brown left that game early because of a hamstring strain and missed the Sixers' next two wins over the Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks . He returned in Monday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers , scoring 20 points. After that game, Brown said he had "a little bit of soreness." "You want to make sure you play it the right way, be safe," he said. "Also, don't want to miss a lot of games, so I want to be out there but also got to be smart. So I think I played it the right way today." Brown is averaging 21.4 points, 6.0 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game. Center Joel Embiid missed Wednesday's game and the loss to the Trail Blazers because of an illness. The Sixers play at the Indiana Pacers on Friday.

stories.title: The Sixers’ NBA Cup dreams come down to Friday
stories.summary: With a win over the Indiana Pacers, the Sixers will win East Group B and advance to the NBA Cup's knockout round for the first time ever.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 15: LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers looks to pass the ball during the game against the Indiana Pacers on November 15, 2026 at the Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images For the first three years of the NBA Cup, the Sixers failed to advance past the group-play stage. This season, they have a chance to make it to the knockout round for the first time ever. Wednesday unfolded exactly how the Sixers needed it to . Despite being without Joel Embiid and losing Jaylen Brown to a hamstring injury in the first half, the Sixers held on to beat the Miami Heat, 111-104. A few hours later, the New York Knicks pasted the Cleveland Cavaliers, 121-102. (Can someone please stick a fork in the Cavs? For their own sake?) Here’s an updated look at the East Group B standings heading into Friday: Team W L Diff Philadelphia 76ers 2 1 -12 Miami Heat 2 1 +24 Cleveland Cavaliers 2 2 +2 Indiana Pacers 1 2 -27 New York Knicks 1 2 +12 For the Sixers, it’s simple: win and they’re in. If they beat the Indiana Pacers, they’ll clinch East Group B no matter what happens in Knicks-Heat. The Knicks already have two losses, and the Sixers now have the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Heat courtesy of Wednesday’s victory. The Cavs have the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Sixers, but that’s no longer an issue since they’re locked in at 2-2. If the Sixers lose to the Pacers, their minus-12 point differential will keep them out of the wild-card mix. You might not think that’s a big deal, but as Joe Flynn noted on Bluesky, the stakes are sneakily high. Given the three-year sample size, you might be inclined to discount that as a meaningful correlation. Fair enough. With that said, there’s also a financial prize for advancing to the knockout round and beyond, which actually is a big deal for a number of players on the Sixers’ roster. This was the financial breakdown last year, according to Colin Salao of Front Office Sports : Advance to the knockout round: $53,093 per player Advance to the semifinals: $106,187 per player Advance to the NBA Cup final: $212,373 per player Win the NBA Cup: $530,933 per player Sure, LeBron James and Joel Embiid might not bat an eye at an extra half-million, but most of their teammates are earning $6 million or less this year. Hell, even LeBron is only earning $3.9 million on his contract. Winning the NBA Cup would be more than a 10 percent bonus! In years past, stars like LeBron, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander have spoken about how their lesser-paid teammates give them extra motivation to advance deep into the Cup’s knockout round. For young players such as Labaron Philon Jr. ($3.6 million), Dominick Barlow ($3.4 million), Ariel Hukporti ($3.4 million), Jabari Walker ($2.6 million) and Adem Bona ($2.3 million), the Cup prize is a hefty portion of their salary. For a basketball history buff like LeBron, there’s extra incentive to reach the Cup final this year. The Cup semifinals and finals were held in Las Vegas in each of the first three years, but the NBA changed it up this year by moving the semifinals to normal NBA team markets and hosting the final at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. LeBron gushed about the Palestra earlier this year, and it’s easy to imagine him getting fired up to play at another iconic non-NBA venue. The Sixers very well might have to beat the Pacers without Brown, who aggravated his hamstring injury and is set to undergo imaging Thursday. If Embiid can return, they’re likely headed for an all-time schedule loss against the Houston Rockets on the second night of a back-to-back Saturday, as both LeBron and Embiid will be more incentivized to suit up against Indiana to clinch a spot in the Cup’s knockout round. If the Sixers take care of business Friday, they’ll earn at least $50,000 per player. Not bad for a day’s worth of work. stories.title: The Lakers will need help to advance in the NBA Cup
stories.summary: A win alone won’t be enough for the Lakers to guarantee a spot in the knockout rounds of the NBA Cup.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 20: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers high fives fans before the game against the Sacramento Kings during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 20, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images In news that should shock no one, the Kings sit at the bottom of Group C in the NBA Cup this year, winless in four games. Above them sit four teams, including the Lakers, at 2-1. Each has a path to advance as we head into Friday, the final day of NBA Cup play, setting up an exciting finish. The Spurs and Lakers will have their anticipated showdown on Friday evening. At the same time, the Warriors and Blazers square off in Portland. All four teams need a win and results going their way in the other game to advance, setting up some good ol’ scoreboard watching during the game. So, let’s look at how the Lakers can win the group and their much slimmer path to a wild card spot. How the Lakers can win the group The Lakers’ desire to beat the Spurs on Friday likely centers on making a statement against arguably the top team in the Western Conference. The added bonus, perhaps, is that they can advance in the NBA Cup as well. Any path out of the group requires a win on Friday. A loss drops them to 2-2 in the group and with two teams guaranteed to finish with just one loss, the Lakers can’t advance as a wild card with a loss. But winning isn’t enough. The Lakers’ loss to the Warriors in Golden State — a game they led by 25 points — leaves them needing help to move on. If LA and Portland both win, the Lakers hold the head-to-head tiebreaker and win the group. However, if Golden State upsets the Blazers in Portland, then that Halloween Eve loss stings a bit more as the Warriors will top the group. Those two-leg scenarios exist for each side. Portland must win and have the Spurs win to win the group while San Antonio needs a victory and a Warriors upset to do the same. However, winning the group isn’t the only way to advance to the knockout rounds. How the Lakers could take the wild card spot Along with the three group winners, one wild card advances to the knockout rounds. For the Lakers, this only comes into play if they win and the Warriors win, leaving them with just one loss in the group. Point differential is how the wild card spot is determined and the Lakers aren’t in an ideal spot. LA’s close win one week ago over the Kings didn’t offset the big loss to the Warriors. As a result, they enter the final game with a -9 point differential. The simplest way for all this to play out is for the Wolves, who may be without LaMelo Ball , to beat the Grizzlies, leaving no one-loss teams in Group B. Then the tiebreaker will be between the Lakers and the Nuggets. Denver has a -3 point differential, but get to play the Jazz, who are winless in the NBA Cup. If both the Nuggets and Lakers win, LA would have to beat Denver’s margin of victory by at least seven points, assuming Denver wins. The potential wrench in these plans is the Grizzlies-Wolves contest. Coming into Friday, Minnesota has a +39 point differential and Memphis is at +18. If the Grizzlies win a close game, then the Wolves likely have the inside track at the wild card spot. It would take a really big Memphis win to bring the Wolves into the point differential range of the Lakers and Nuggets. These wild card races always have so many moving parts, so here’s perhaps the simplest rooting guide for Friday: Lakers blowout win vs. Spurs Blazers win vs. Warriors If Blazers lose… Denver close win or loss at Jazz Grizzlies huge blowout win or loss at Wolves You can follow Jacob on Twitter at @JacobRude or on Bluesky at @jacobrude.bsky.social .

stories.title: Timberwolves' LaMelo Ball limps off vs. OKC after hurting left ankle
stories.summary: The Timberwolves did not have an update on the status of LaMelo Ball's left ankle after he was injured late in a win over the Thunder.
stories.detailText: OKLAHOMA CITY -- Minnesota Timberwolves star guard LaMelo Ball exited late in the fourth quarter of Wednesday night's 113-106 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder after turning his left ankle. Ball had to be helped off the court with 2:29 remaining after he landed on one of Thunder center Isaiah Hartenstein 's feet. Ball was briefly evaluated on the bench before hobbling to the locker room as the Timberwolves held a one-point lead. Timberwolves coach Chris Finch did not have any information about the severity of Ball's injury immediately after the win. "It looked pretty bad, but I'm not sure," Finch said. Ball, who had 19 points and eight assists, did not speak to the media postgame. He was upbeat in the locker room, laughing and joking with teammates as he iced his feet and ankles. Acquired in an offseason trade with the Charlotte Hornets , Ball has been a driving force in the Timberwolves' early-season success. Minnesota (14-5) is tied for third in the Western Conference despite perennial All-Star shooting guard Anthony Edwards being sidelined since undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery after the opening week of the season. There isn't a firm timetable for Edwards' return, but he is expected to miss several more weeks. Timberwolves guard Ayo Dosunmu (16 points, 4 assists) had a driving layup and 3-pointer in Minnesota's next two possessions after Ball was injured to key the closeout of the Thunder. Forward Jaden McDaniels had another spectacular performance, finishing with 32 points, 10 rebounds and five assists while also serving as the primary defender on back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (32 points, 13-of-26 shooting). According to ESPN Insights, McDaniels joined Kevin Garnett and Karl-Anthony Towns as the only players in franchise history with consecutive 30-point, 10-rebound, five-assist outings. "He's a star," Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert said. "He's one of the best two-way players in the league."

stories.summary: LeBron took over and scored 14 straight points in the second quarter.

LeBron James has got this, no problem. LeBron James scored 14 STRAIGHT points in the 2Q en route to his first triple-double as a Sixer 25 PTS | 10 REB | 12 AST | 9-15 FGM | 4-6 3PM Philly moved to 2-1 in @emirates NBA Cup Group Play to stay in contention to win East Group B! pic.twitter.com/5GubFnJi9L — NBA (@NBA) November 26, 2026 LeBron had a 25-point triple-double — including scoring 14 straight in the second quarter — to lift the 76ers to a 111-104 NBA Cup win at home. But right now, he’s giving Father Time hell," Heat coach (and former LeBron coach) Erik Spoelstra said before the game. This has been an impressive start from the 76ers, who are 15-4 and comfortably atop the Eastern Conference. They're also 2-1 in NBA Cup Group B play and can win the group and advance to the knockout round by beating Indiana on Friday night.

stories.summary: Wagner's efficiency and Wolf's shooting have given Brooklyn two unexpected offensive weapons.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 04: Danny Wolf #2 of the Brooklyn Nets in action during the game against the Charlotte Hornets at Barclays Center on November 04, 2026 in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. The Nets won 114-104. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s pretty doom and gloom in NetsWorld right now, and that’s justified. Sitting at 3-13 after Monday night’s blowout against the Minnesota Timberwolves, the team has now suffered nine double-digit losses this season. When a young, rebuilding team isn’t winning, it’s one thing, but getting completely outmatched consistently is another. That’s pretty much what’s been the case for Brooklyn, as nine of their 13 losses have come by 10+ points. Interestingly, one of the biggest questions entering the season surrounded Brooklyn’s frontcourt. It wasn’t clear how the rotation would take shape. Day’Ron Sharpe entered the season as the team’s starting center following Nic Claxton’s departure, while Moe Wagner arrived in free agency. Wagner’s health was in question after he played just 66 games over the previous two seasons, including time missed due to a torn ACL. Danny Wolf was another question mark after an up-and-down rookie campaign. So far, the frontcourt has produced more offense than expected. Brooklyn’s rim protection remains a work in progress, and its defense has struggled at every level. But offensively, two of the team’s biggest surprises have been Wagner and Wolf. Offensively, two of Brooklyn’s biggest surprises have been Wagner and Wolf. Wagner is picking up where he left off. Wagner has been known for his offensive game since entering the league—most notably his success from beyond the arc and his consistency. Although injuries have hindered him significantly over the past two years, Wagner is starting to pick up where he left off before the ACL injury forced him out of action for 98 games. Through 16 games, Wagner owns a 70.7% effective field-goal percentage, ranking in the 98th percentile among bigs, per Cleaning the Glass. A large part of that production comes from his remarkable 62.5% shooting from three-point range. That percentage almost certainly won’t hold over an 82-game season, but it’s an encouraging start to his Brooklyn tenure. Moe buckets‼️🪣 pic.twitter.com/hg9lqu9a51 — Brooklyn Nets (@BrooklynNets) October 28, 2026 What’s even more encouraging, though, is the success beyond just the 3-point line. For a big like Wagner, who isn’t necessarily touted for rim protection or stout defense, being a multi-faceted offensive contributor is crucial. Worth noting, though, he only played four minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Milwaukee Bucks after exiting with left knee soreness. Overall, he’s returning to the offense that worked at the peak of his career in Orlando. Last season with the Magic, just 44% of his overall attempts came at the rim, while 25% came from the midrange. This year, those numbers have shifted to 60% and 19%, respectively. That’s much more in line with what we saw from Wagner during his two most efficient seasons (2023-24, 2024-25), with his effective FG percentage finishing north of 60% in both of those campaigns. MOE ENERGY 😤 pic.twitter.com/TnkZndEcbg — Brooklyn Nets (@BrooklynNets) November 12, 2026 Wagner has also improved drastically at creating his own shot. Last season, 88% of his made baskets at the rim were assisted. Meanwhile, that has dropped to 61%, despite a 15-percentage-point increase in his shot usage around the basket. Obviously, there’s only so much that Wagner could be expected to do. Signed to a two-year, $18.4 million contract this offseason, he was widely viewed as the Nets’ backup big behind Sharpe. So far, that has held. Sharpe has started all 17 of Brooklyn’s games, while averaging 24 minutes per game. Meanwhile, off the bench, Wagner has averaged 17.1 minutes a game. Moe Wagner at the break 📊 13 PTS 5-7 FG 2-2 3FG pic.twitter.com/3idZCCW4MG — Brooklyn Nets (@BrooklynNets) October 25, 2026 Entering the season, one of the biggest concerns with the Nets’ roster was where points would come from off the bench. So far, their bench scoring hasn’t been too shabby, ranking 13th in bench points per game (38.7). More impressively, though, their bench ranks 11th in 3-point percentage (35.7%). Wagner is clearly a big reason behind that. Having a big who can stretch the floor while also generating offense around the basket is a luxury. Wolf is establishing his offensive identity The bigger question mark entering the year is what the Nets really had in Wolf. Just like the four Flatbush 5 members behind Egor Dëmin, whose start to the year had been disappointing, the Michigan product had a lot to prove heading into the season. So far, though, that development has been encouraging. Just like Wagner, the 27th overall pick in last June’s draft has emerged as a threat from beyond the arc. After shooting just 32% from deep as a rookie, he is converting at 46.7% this season, ranking in the 95th percentile among bigs. There has also been an uptick in volume: 54% of his overall shot attempts have come from the 3-point range, up from 44% a season ago. His mark this year ranks in the 88th percentile among bigs. Beyond that, 35% of his overall attempts have come from non-corner 3s, which ranks in the 91st percentile. Wolf’s output has also had a large impact on Brooklyn as a whole. Last season, the Nets scored 5.1 fewer points per 100 possessions with him on the floor than with him on the bench. This season, they’re scoring 5.4 more points per 100 possessions with him out there, ranking in the 83rd percentile among all players. Danny Wolf full highlights vs. Minnesota Timberwolves tonight (142-116 L): 11 Points on 4/7 FG (57.1%), 3/5 from 3 (60.0%), 5 Rebounds, 4 Assists (ZERO turnovers), 1 Block, 2 fouls, and a +/- of -6 in 25:03 minutes played. Despite the defeat, he became one of the most reliable… pic.twitter.com/mtFjPEqbzC — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) November 24, 2026 Additionally, the Nets’ effective field-goal percentage improves by 3.2 percentage points with him on the floor, while the offensive rebounding percentage also rises by 8.3 percentage points. The latter ranks in the 96th percentile among players who have logged a minute this season. For context, he has only played 244 minutes this season, but those numbers are still fascinating. Even more interesting is how he’s been used. After opening the season outside of Jordi Fernández’s rotation, Wolf has worked his way into the lineup, but in an odd spot: as the Nets’ starting shooting guard. How many people had that on their bingo card entering the season? In fact, six of his seven starts this season have come at the 2. Against the Magic on Friday night, Fernández inserted Wolf into the starting five for Dëmin, and Wolf responded with a 20-point outing. In his second straight start, against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday, he finished with 11 points, four assists, and five rebounds on 4-of-7 shooting, including 3-of-5 from deep. https://t.co/iVpcfykg7G pic.twitter.com/pSXXJ5pZcP — Brooklyn Nets (@BrooklynNets) November 21, 2026 As our own Anthony Puccio noted earlier this month, Wolf played every second of his initial breakout performance against the Charlotte Hornets alongside either Sharpe or Wagner. That trend has held mostly true since then, letting him work away from the basket and avoid many traditional big responsibilities. Is he truly a 5 in the NBA? There need to be more reps to make the case for or against it, but he doesn’t ideally fit as a shooting guard. At 6’11”, it’s just not a natural fit, and it is easy for him to get exposed guarding shifty playmaking guards at the top of the key. Even though he was a ball handler at Michigan, being a guard in college versus the NBA are two completely different responsibilities. Nonetheless, the versatility is highly encouraging. Regardless of where Wolf ultimately settles in the long term, he and Wagner have given the Nets more offensively than anyone could have asked for before the season.

stories.title: Friday Night Lights,' 'Ted Lasso' top poll ranking 21st-century sports shows
stories.summary: A Seton Hall poll crowns America's favorite modern fictional sports TV series.﻿
stories.detailText: It's been quite the year for scripted sports series, with milestones worth celebrating and new chapters worthy of clearing space on the couch. "Friday Night Lights" hit its two-decade anniversary. "One Tree Hill" turned 23 -- a number Nathan Scott and Michael Jordan would both approve of. On the more modern side, "Ted Lasso" returned for its fourth season , while "All American" wrapped up its Season 8 series finale. Through different eras and sports, fans have plenty of reasons to get invested, so we tapped Seton Hall for a poll on America's favorite sports show of the 21st century. "Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" took the top spots among the general population at 16% and 15%, respectively. The Texas-based football drama also held the edge among avid sports fans, 25% to 22%, and casual sports fans, 23% to 18%. "The two leaders in the clubhouse for top series indicate that depth and consistency resonate the most with all sports fans," said Len DeLuca, associate director, Seton Hall Sports Poll and instructor in the Seton Hall Stillman Center for sport management. "'Friday Night Lights' was on NBC 14 years before 'Ted Lasso' premiered on Apple TV. This proves that sports content is agnostic to platform." Whether your loyalty lies with the Dillon Panthers, the Tree Hill Ravens or AFC Richmond, there's a good chance your favorite fictional team has put you through highs and lows. And much like rooting for a real team, picking a favorite show can inspire a spirited debate. Here are the key findings. Football leads a multisport lineup Among the general population, "Friday Night Lights" led all shows at 16%, with "All American" at 10%, "The Game" at 8% and "Ballers" at 7%. That gave football four of the eight highest-polling series overall. Viewers had plenty of interest in the drama surrounding the game, from high school rivalries to the business of professional sports. Still, football didn't sweep the podium: Soccer's "Ted Lasso" and karate's "Cobra Kai" finished second and third at 15% and 13%, respectively. With 12%, "A League of Their Own" added representation for baseball and took the fourth spot. Hockey's "The Mighty Ducks: Game Changers" and basketball's "One Tree Hill" also drew 7% each, matching "Ballers." The generation gap The age ranges didn't differ entirely, but different generations tended to root for different fictional teams. 18-34: "Ted Lasso" led with 17%, followed by "All American," "The Game" and "The English Game" at 14% each. Newer titles also found an audience here: "Heated Rivalry" drew 10%, its strongest showing across the age groups. 35-54: This group showed the most love for "Cobra Kai," which topped its list at 19%. "Friday Night Lights" followed at 18%, with "Ted Lasso" at 15%. "One Tree Hill" and "Eastbound & Down" also had their strongest showings here at 10% each. 55+: "Friday Night Lights" took the lead at 17%, narrowly ahead of "A League of Their Own" at 16%. "Ted Lasso" rounded out the top three at 13%. The drop-off was sharper for teen dramas such as "All American" and "One Tree Hill," which drew 5% and 3%, respectively. Commonalities and contrasts between sports fans and nonfans Sports fans and nonfans found some common ground, even if they weren't watching the same shows. "Friday Night Lights" led among sports fans at 23%, followed by "Ted Lasso" at 19% and "Cobra Kai" and "A League of Their Own" at 16% each. Among nonfans, "Cobra Kai" moved into first at 8%, with "Ted Lasso" and "A League of Their Own" tied at 7%. Coach Eric Taylor (played by Kyle Chandler) had a tougher time with that crowd, as "Friday Night Lights" drew 5%. The biggest divide, though, was in those who selected "don't know/no opinion": 69% of nonfans compared with 28% of sports fans. The crossover appeal is there, but viewers with less interest in sports need more motivation to tune in. The men's and women's lineups look a little different "Friday Night Lights" and "Ted Lasso" finished first and second among both men and women, but the order differs after that. Among men, "Cobra Kai" took third at 15%, followed by "A League of Their Own" at 11%. Women flipped those two, with "A League of Their Own" drawing 14% and "Cobra Kai" at 11%. "Make It or Break It" and "Heated Rivalry" also drew higher percentages among women than men, both at 6% to 4%. New shows are earning their stripes Some newer series are already finding a place alongside the familiar favorites. "Chad Powers" drew 6% overall, followed by "Heated Rivalry" at 5% and "Running Point" and "Off Campus" at 4% each. For avid sports fans, "Chad Powers" reached 13%, matching "The Game" in that group. "Heated Rivalry," meanwhile, had its strongest showing among adults ages 18-34 at 10%. The established shows have a head start, but the newcomers are getting some playing time. Editor's Note: These results are derived from a Seton Hall Sports Poll conducted Oct. 8 to Oct. 13, 2026, among 1,632 adults. The Poll, which is sponsored by The Sharkey Institute within Seton Hall University's Stillman School of Business, features a national representative sample from YouGov Plc., weighted on U.S. Census Bureau figures for age, gender, ethnicity, education, income and geography with a margin of error of +/- 3.0 percent.

stories.title: The stealing, running Mavs are the perfect cast for a high-IQ duo that could change basketball
stories.summary: The Dallas Mavericks are now the exact opposite of who they used to be.
stories.detailText: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 24: Kyrie Irving #11 and Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks shake hands during the third quarter against the Denver Nuggets at Ball Arena on November 24, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by C. Morgan Engel/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Mavericks just beat a very good Denver Nuggets team through aggressive defense, forcing steals, and running on offense. It is indeed a new day in Dallas. Kyrie Irving, a player that has pretty much seen it all by now, didn’t even have an efficient night (5/19 on field goal attempts, 1/8 from three). He did, however, lead the team to a victory that shows the whole league that the Dallas Mavericks now are the exact opposite of who they used to be. In a gesture as moving as it was telling, Kyrie showed the world that he and Cooper Flagg have the rarest of connections. This is a high-IQ duo who could change the trajectory of what basketball looks like. And they may be on the way to doing that as we speak. It is not only the gesture that’s important here, it’s the ultimate look away pass and the back door cut by Flagg that shows a connection between the two, usually built through years of ups and downs. It was almost like they could read each other’s minds. This is what real chemistry looks like. Jamal Crawford: "Watch Kyrie Irving telling Cooper, me and you!" KAI & COOP'S CHEMISTRY ON DISPLAY IN DENVER 🙌 pic.twitter.com/cgWrIA156h — NBA (@NBA) November 25, 2026 Kirk Henderson said it best: “There are lookaway passes, then there’s something like this where I feel as if Kyrie’s head never even moved the direction where Coop cut to.” Jamal Crawford interpreted the gesture as “me and you”, and either way this is a gesture of connection, we – as in us – we got this . And even though Kyrie meant Cooper, we all feel it a little bit. You may be watching from across the globe, you may not even be a Mavs fan, but anybody watching, knowing what this team and city have gone through recently, felt it. Because no one has worked harder to get the Dallas Mavericks back together than Kyrie Irving. After it was torn apart, he did everything he could to hold it together. He mentored, he was everyone’s vet, he led, he coached when injured – he showed the way and the light in the dark times. And Dallas is reaping the benefits right now. That is also why it felt so touching, seeing the vet who worked so hard to hold it all together, make this gesture to the young superstar with the highest ceiling imaginable. They took away his running mate, his brother and a genuine friendship and on-court chemistry, resulting in the most negative period in Dallas, in which he forced himself to play too much and carry more than he should have. His resulting ACL injury took him away from his craft for more than a year, and now – finally – his hard work is really paying off. Kyrie Irving deserves this. And despite the spiritual experience it can be to watch Irving play, especially when he has chemistry with his teammates, he didn’t carry the team to this extraordinary win. Neither did his co-star Flagg really. It was a cast of teammates who decided to outwork, outhustle and believe in their connection, along with a well-prepared coach, who had clearly done a lot of work to get this team ready. It was no easy feat. But the Mavs made it look easy. They had 13 steals. The league leader averages 10.6 (Los Angeles Lakers). The Mavs average 9.44 this season, but led by the surprising hero of the last games, Caleb Martin, with five, they kept the pressure on the passing lanes all game, stressing the Nuggets in a way we don’t see every day. Not only that, they had 16 steals last game versus Utah, and a whopping 50 steals the last four games (which all happen to be wins). Martin started this game on fire on both ends, secured the first six points by knocking down two threes in a row and continued to force five steals in the first half, constantly the first to run in transition. CALEB MARTIN THROWDOWN ON THE BREAK! DAL-DEN • West Group A 🏆 @emirates NBA Cup on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/SBs9dF7RYS — NBA (@NBA) November 25, 2026 This is exactly the leadership a team needs from a role player next to superstars, and with Zaccharie Risacher next to him, the two have the potential to cause havoc defensively on every team in the league, followed by easy transition points, if they keep this up. Caleb Martin explained the game plan in the half: “High sense of urgency. A high level of respect for a great team,” he said during the broadcast. He went on to explain that steals were an emphasis, as well as just being active. “The more active we are,” Martin said, “sense of urgency, the better a team we are, positive things happen”. And not even interview questions were about to distract Caleb Martin, who is on a mission in Dallas right now. When asked in the half whether the loud colors of the court, which are usually a little on the bright side during Cup games, was giving him a headache, too, he answered deadpan: “I don’t know, I’m trying to win a game right now.” Find more Beyond Basketball pieces here.

Here are very few quotes from yesterday’s affair and elsewhere. Enjoy Thanksgiving today, and make sure to save the leftovers! . @Krisplashed : "You started 0-3. Now you're 12-6" Mike Brown: "Our sht still does stink" pic.twitter.com/X4Pqm7BKRA — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 26, 2026 Mike Brown On the benefits of potentially missing the NBA Cup knockout rounds: “It is important (to win and potentially advance), but the reality of it is, when you look at the schedule, and you see that our percentage [to advance] is not that high, and so they kind of shared with me what our schedule would look like if we don’t go and if we do go. And you look at it, you’re like, ‘Whoa, that’s a lot of days off if you don’t go.’ And so again, you want to compete; you want to win. But if you don’t, in my opinion, when you look at the schedule… you’re like, there’s an opportunity if you got some guys banged up to get rest and/or to work on some things in between the games that you have if you’re not involved in the Cup.” On the physical and mental toll of competing in the NBA Cup: “I didn’t really break it down to an 83rd game, but when I talk about the Cup, it adds a level of stress maybe on your mind and your body because the games are intense as you go along and you’re playing more games in a short amount of time. “I remember it was like, game, game, game, and then you win the Cup, and you celebrate it that night, and you hop on a plane and go play in Indiana the next night. And so it’s great. You like the competition and the setup, but it adds a lot of stress to you physically and mentally. I’m saying this because especially with the extended season we had last year and how taxing the games were for our playoff run mentally and physically, I’m trying to be smart, so if — knock on wood — we end up advancing, I’ll try to be smart about it.” On refusing to chase regular-season wins at all costs and learning from Golden State’s 73-win season: “I try not to chase wins, especially early in the season. You want to win, but I’m not going to win every game at all costs. “I wasn’t part of the staff [for the first Golden State title] [Golden State] won Steve [Kerr’s] first year. Then they lost in the second year, but they set a regular season record of 73 wins, and one of the things that he used to tell me, they gassed themselves trying to get this record and come playoff time they just didn’t have enough in the tank to close it. And so that always sits right here for me.” On calling Pacôme Dadiet into his office and threatening to remove him from the rotation over his lack of effort: “I didn’t think he played hard in the game before. And I actually called him into my office and showed him some film. I told him, ‘As a young guy, if you don’t play hard, I can’t play you.’ “And I said, ‘Believe me, I got a lot of guys I can go to. I’m not afraid to go to somebody else. So the least you could do is play hard.’ And I showed him how he wasn’t. And I thought [Wednesday], he played hard.” On leaving OG Anunoby’s injury management to the medical staff: “There are a lot of medical terms that are above my head. They tell me and I don’t really pick up on the injury. If he’s out, I change my minutes sheet. And then I’ll just wait for them to tell me when he’s back. [Wednesday], OG’s individual work happened before shootaround and I didn’t even know he had individual work until his player development guy told me later on. You never want a guy to hurt himself more. But I don’t think about it.” On the Knicks still having plenty of room for improvement despite winning 12 of their last 15 games: “We’re 12-3 since the start, but our s–t still does stink. We haven’t arrived, and we still have to embrace the little things.” Josh Hart: "Black Tyler came in and gave great energy" @alanhahn : "You called him what?" Josh: "Black Tyler. Yeah. We have White Tyler and Black Tyler. That was Black Tyler" @Krisplashed : "What's the difference between them?" Josh: "Have you heard them talk?" pic.twitter.com/71c5WOuSkI — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 26, 2026 Josh Hart On Brown experimenting with an unusually deep rotation against Cleveland: “I looked at the bench in the first quarter and realized, ‘Wow, we played like 10 people in that first quarter.’” Karl-Anthony Towns On endorsing Tom Thibodeau as a potential head coaching hire for struggling NBA franchises: “I made three playoffs with Thibodeau as my coach so his track record is one of success. So of course if I was a team that wanted to get back on track, I’d look at Tom Thibodeau to be my coach.” On Thibodeau’s tactical knowledge, dedication and ability to prepare his teams to win: “It’s the X’s and O’s and the amount of care he puts into his craft, his team. He steps into that gym every day and, you know, you can say anything you want about the way he coaches, but one thing I know is his team is prepared to win a game. So that’s a testament to who he is as a coach, the preparation he puts his team through and also his ability to have his team ready for the moment.” Kevin Durant and Dillon Brooks literally STOPPED playing basketball mid play to square up. That’s real hate 😂😂 pic.twitter.com/WSxwt5vdbi — Hater Report (@HaterReport) November 26, 2026

(Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images stoneAge: Did you expect the rebuild to take so long and how far away are the Nets from being a playoff team again? AP : I expected it to take long, but I figured they would have moved some assets to speed this thing up. I was wrong. We’re looking at a Nets team currently two-three years away from playoffs—and that’s being generous. stoneAge: Which of the Nets’ current players are part of their future core and what do the Nets lack the most to reach the next level? AP : Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Dëmin, and Nolan Traore. The Nets lack a lot of things, particularly size in the front court. This isn’t new. They lack athleticism. They lack three-point shooters. And they lack basic fundamentals required to build on good habits for a sustainable culture. Mitchell Maurer: How do you navigate a landscape where so many people in the same geographic area are head-over-heels for the Knicks? A title is (as we’ve seen around here…) a surefire way to attract bandwagon fans, who are as vocal as they are anonymous ’round these Internet parts. The Nets are not a “nothing” franchise but they clearly don’t carry the same weight (broadly speaking) as their cross-town counterparts. It’s not a fair paradigm, to be considered an “afterthought” and I’m curious if there’s similarities with how Bucks fans may have felt back in the heyday of the Packers and/or Brewers (who also just won a title!) AP : Nets fans don’t want to admit it, but there’s absolutely an inferiority. Before the Knicks’ chip, the one thing Nets fans had on Knicks fans was a better on-court product since 2000. Now we don’t even have that! Put it this way: if you tell someone you’re a Nets fan in NY, depending on who you tell, they might say, “Who?” Or “Why?” Navigating Expectations BOSTON, MA – MAY 30: James Harden #13, Kevin Durant #7, and Kyrie Irving #11 of the Brooklyn Nets look on during Round 1, Game 4 of the 2021 NBA Playoffs on May 30, 2021 at the TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Grant Burke/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Terrapin Revisited: What was it like to adjust expectations when the Nets went from title contenders to “Well, what exactly are we now?” after their big trades? Any recommendations for Bucks fans on how to adapt? AP : There’s no way of sugar-coating it—it feels like a dead end. You adapt when you simply learn to accept this is the new reality, and you never know when it might return. My recommendation: lean on the community to talk. It’s difficult without picks to look forward to. Expect the worst, hope the best. Don’t turn on each other though. ( Editor’s note: Sage advice—and one of the things I love about Brew Hoop ). Terrapin Revisited: What have you enjoyed most about the Nets during this rebuilding era? In other words, what can fans focus on as far as the bright side of such teams? AP : Watching people in the organization make a name for themselves, hustling and shining in the shadows of the down years. Ideally it a player, but it can be any personnel. College basketball, too. A number of Bucks’ vets are disappointing this year, I’m not sure how much that is to be expected when the stakes they are playing for are a lot lower vs. how much that provides some useful insights on the vets. stories.title: LeBron James dusts 'off the cape' to save 76ers with triple-double
stories.summary: The soon-to-be 42-year-old LeBron James showed his ability to put the 76ers on his back with a 25-point triple-double in Wednesday's NBA Cup win over the Heat.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- While LeBron James has maintained it's not his job to dominate every night for the talent-rich 76ers , he showed his ability to still play savior when needed. James had his best game of the season in the Sixers' 111-104 win over the Miami Heat (10-7) in Wednesday night's NBA Cup matchup, finishing with a season-high 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds. The victory snapped the Heat's seven-game winning streak and moved the Sixers to 15-4 on the season. "I don't think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ballclub," James said. "... If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that. But that's not my job. "But if they need it, I can do it at any given moment." That moment came in the second quarter Wednesday, as James decided to take over, scoring 14 straight points for the 76ers, which included three 3-pointers from well beyond the arc. On James' third 3-pointer, which gave the Sixers a six-point lead, he strutted down to one end of the Xfinity Mobile Arena with a smirk and nodded his head. James has found a rhythm over the Sixers' past two games with his highest scoring totals of the season: 23 against the Portland Trail Blazers and 25 against the Heat. But where his game has taken the biggest leap is beyond the arc: James is 8-for-11 from 3 over his past two games. He was 10-for-46 (22%) over his first 13 games. 76ers coach Nick Nurse said James' long-range shooting was the most impressive part of Wednesday's performance. "I kind of know when my hand is feeling pretty good," James said, "especially from the outside." James' play has fluctuated this season. For as good as he has been in the past two games, there are performances such as his eight-point outing against the Cleveland Cavaliers earlier this month, when shot 3-for-12 and had six turnovers. Or days later against the Boston Celtics when he was 4-for-12 with 11 points and a minus-17 rating. James chalks that up to his age. "About to be 42 years old in a month. S---, it takes a little bit longer for the ramp up," he said. "But I'll never be second guessing myself or whatever the case may be because I know the work I put in." James' performance was welcomed from guard Tyrese Maxey , who led Philadelphia with 30 points. After hearing James saying he can dust off his cape, Maxey yelled: "Dust it off then." "He knows when he needs to score. He knows when he needs to pass," Maxey said. "We're going to need a lot from him. I know he's seasoned, but we expect a lot of him and he does that." Philadelphia won this game without Joel Embiid , who was out with an illness , and one half without Jaylen Brown , who exited the game with left hamstring tightness . Nurse said Brown will get imaging. He didn't have an update on Embiid. The Sixers will play the Pacers in Indiana on Friday in the final game of NBA Cup group play. With a win, the 76ers will clinch Eastern Conference Group B and advance to the knockout rounds for the first time in franchise history.

stories.title: Observations after James posts triple-double, Sixers beat Heat in NBA Cup
stories.summary: James registered 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds as he helped to lead the Sixers to an important NBA Cup win.
stories.detailText: Observations after James posts triple-double, Sixers beat Heat in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James posted his first triple-double as a Sixer on Wednesday night and led his team to a 111-104 win over the Heat at Xfinity Mobile Arena. James notched his 126th career regular-season triple-double with 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for the 15-4 Sixers. Tyrese Maxey scored 30 points and dished out six assists. Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 32 points and 14 rebounds for the 10-7 Heat. The Sixers improved to 2-1 and Miami fell to 2-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup. Jaylen Brown was ruled out at halftime with left hamstring tightness. He had six points on 2-for-8 shooting over 17 minutes. “He’ll get some imaging and we’ll get the update tomorrow,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. Joel Embiid (illness) missed his second game in a row. The Sixers are set to visit the Pacers on Friday night in their final Cup group game. “He’s ill,” Nurse said of Embiid. “I do not know whether he’s going to Indiana yet or not. I guess we’ll find that out late tomorrow afternoon.” Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory over the Heat: Early trouble against Antetokounmpo Nurse emphasized pregame that the Sixers needed an improved defensive performance. “We’ve got to compete much better at the defensive end than we did Monday (against the Trail Blazers) ,” he said. “It’s as simple as that.” The night did not begin in especially promising fashion on that front. Antetokounmpo powered through Brown and scored inside for the game’s first bucket. His transition layup put Miami up 6-0. The Heat scored nine fast-break points in the first six minutes. As he had Monday in the Sixers’ loss to Portland, Jabari Walker started at center. He was among the Sixers who shared the daunting defensive assignment of Antetokounmpo. Walker took a charge on the 10-time All-Star in the first quarter, but Antetounkmpo had a stellar start. He forcefully orchestrated Miami’s offense, often plowing through the middle of the floor and finding efficient answers. James stays hot The Sixers’ defense was better late in the first quarter and it didn’t hurt when Antetokounmpo took a seat. Maxey had an aggressive, productive first period, scoring 13 points. Dominick Barlow’s tip-in gave the Sixers a 27-26 edge. James drained three three-pointers early in the second quarter, including a confident, deep jumper that fired up a high-volume home crowd. He’s shown that he remains capable of flipping a world-class switch and taking over games in a vast array of ways. There’s no question the 22-time All-Star is out of his early-season outside shooting slump. James has gone 8 for 11 from long range over his last two games. He’s scored at least 20 points in four straight. “I just play the game as it unfolds,” James said. “I had a couple of opportunities and I was able to connect on them. I kind of know when my hand is feeling pretty good, especially from the outside. We’ll see how long I can keep it going.” Sixers polish it off Adem Bona checked in early in the second quarter. He provided a string of excellent defensive possessions against Antetokounmpo, including an emphatic block and several well-guarded missed jumpers, although Bona did get called for three fouls in the second period. Nurse was pleased with what he received defensively from both Bona (two blocks, six rebounds) and Barlow (nine points, eight rebounds) off the bench. “They used their gifts,” he said. “They’re quick side to side, both of them. When they’re in that kind of fighting mode like that … they did a good job. We tried to get Bona in there when Giannis was in, just for the rim protection. And Dom just played really, really (well) all over the place … on the defense, on the rebounding, on the running, on the cutting.” The Sixers played effective zone defense at the tail end of the second quarter and held a nine-point halftime lead. That grew as high as 16 points in the third quarter. Miami pulled back within single digits, but the Sixers maintained a healthy advantage and James kept on making highlight plays. He lobbed the ball up to Edgecombe early in the fourth quarter and the second-year guard skied high to lay it in. James later connected with Barlow on an alley-oop. Once the Sixers have a substantial lead, James’ presence is a massive help offensively. He’s very well-accustomed to conducting methodical half-court offense, identifying favorable matchups and turning to fruitful actions over and over. James will also still steam forward on the fast break when he sees the chance. Maxey buried a step-back three to extend his team’s lead to 111-95 with 2:29 on the clock and the Sixers polished off a professional win. The fans roared when James snatched the rebound required to reach his triple-double. “We came out tonight with a different mentality, different energy,” Maxey said. “Nurse got on us a little bit in the film (session) yesterday. He lit a fire for a lot of us, which is good. We needed it.”

stories.title: James can still take over ‘any given moment,' and Sixers trust he'll pick right spots
stories.summary: “If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, then I can still accomplish that,” LeBron James said Wednesday.
stories.detailText: James can still take over ‘any given moment,' and Sixers trust he'll pick right spots originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James isn’t oblivious to the calendar and the clock. He knows he’ll turn 42 years old next month, he’s ancient by NBA standards and decline is inevitable. James also knows who he is and what he still can do, whatever the norms are for players of a certain age. “I think his battle against Father Time is one of the most impressive things he’s done over the course of his entire career,” Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra said Wednesday before Miami’s loss to the Sixers. “We all know and everybody always says that Father Time always wins. But right now he’s giving Father Time hell.” James went on to record his first triple-double with the 15-4 Sixers , posting 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds. The four-time MVP is at 126 regular-season triple-doubles and counting in his career. Only Russell Westbrook, Nikola Jokic, Oscar Robertson and Magic Johnson have more in NBA history. James is 17 above Philadelphia native and Sixers legend Wilt Chamberlain. With Joel Embiid sidelined by illness for a second consecutive game and Jaylen Brown ruled out at halftime with left hamstring tightness, James’ do-it-all performance was timely. Tyrese Maxey’s 30-point, six-assist outing was essential, too. “I’m just trying to play the game the right way,” James said. “I don’t think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ball club. We have a Finals MVP (Brown), we have a regular-season MVP (Embiid), we have an up-and-coming superstar at point guard, we’ve got a young fella in VJ (Edgecombe) who’s up and coming as well. “My dues are paid with what I’ve done. If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, then I can still accomplish that. But that’s not my job. … But if they need it, I can do it at any given moment.” James’ night featured a flurry of very deep three-pointers in the second quarter. He started the season 10 for 46 beyond the arc (21.7 percent), but his percentage has risen to 31.6 with two sweet-shooting games in a row. “The work has been put in and I’m not ever worried about anything as far as my game,” he said. “The difference between the start of the season and now is that my legs are feeling better, my ramp-up is feeling better. “I’m about to be 42 years old in a month. S—, it takes a little bit longer for the ramp-up, but I’ve been feeling pretty good as of late. I don’t ever second-guess myself … because I know the work that I put in.” While James’ rebounding was perhaps the least spectacular aspect of his game, Sixers head coach Nick Nurse appreciated his work on the boards. James has remained a statistically solid defensive rebounder into his 40s and he’s one reason why the Sixers have made a major improvement in that department. According to Cleaning the Glass , the Sixers’ opponents have grabbed 28.4 percent of their own misses, which ranks sixth in the NBA. The team ranked 27th last season. Asked about James’ cape comments, Maxey shouted out, “Dust it off then!” with a grin. Maxey’s not sure exactly when James will dramatically elevate his game, but he trusts the 22-time All-Star to pick the right spots. “I don’t know,” Maxey said. “Early in the game, he was telling me he was tired. I said, ‘Well, we don’t have time for you to be tired.’ “But he does a good job of just managing the game. He knows when he needs to score, he knows when he needs to pass. We’re going to need a lot from him. I know he’s seasoned , but we expect a lot of him and he does that.”

stories.title: Embiid sidelined for Sixers-Blazers with illness
stories.summary: The Sixers ruled Joel Embiid out with an illness Monday night.
stories.detailText: Embiid sidelined for Sixers-Blazers with illness originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers ruled star center Joel Embiid out with an illness Monday night for their game against the Trail Blazers at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Embiid first popped up on the Sixers’ injury report at 11:45 a.m. ET when the team listed him as questionable. He was downgraded to out about 90 minutes before the 7 p.m. tip-off. The 32-year-old big man played in the 14 of the Eastern Conference-leading Sixers ’ first 17 games and averaged 20.4 points, 8.9 rebounds and 4.1 assists. He was the team’s top scorer in each of the last three games and finished one assist shy of a 26-point triple-double Saturday in the Sixers’ win over the Bucks. The Sixers entered Monday 2-1 this season in games without Embiid. They were 21-23 last year. Outside of Embiid, the Sixers are in good shape health-wise. Jalen Brown, Dean Wade and Adem Bona are all set to return from injuries against Portland. Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) is out indefinitely. The Sixers went with a starting five of Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Brown, LeBron James and Jabari Walker. It’s the second start of the year for Walker, who spent his first three NBA seasons with the Blazers and has been an early-season bright spot off the Sixers’ bench.

The Sixers on Thursday night listed Brown as out because of “left hamstring injury management” for their NBA Cup game Friday in Indiana against the Pacers. Joel Embiid (illness) was listed as questionable after missing the last two games. Brown’s hamstring has been problematic of late. He also played Wednesday in the team’s victory against the Heat , but Brown was ruled out at halftime with an issue the Sixers described as “left hamstring tightness.” “He’ll get some imaging and we’ll get the update tomorrow,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said after the game.
