While Jones possibly chose to take the high road, a former employer vouching for a coach is fundamentally different than his current employer vouching for him. McCarthy took the Cowboys to the playoffs three times in five years, advancing to the divisional round in 2022. The Cowboys failed to qualify for the postseason in the first year after McCarthy left. Thursday's loss to the Eagles makes it harder for them to get there the second post-McCarthy season.

stories.title: QB Caleb Williams, WR Rome Odunze's chemistry helps Bears stun Lions
stories.summary: QB Caleb Williams and WR Rome Odunze leaned on their chemistry trust to secure Chicago's ninth win of the season.
stories.detailText: DETROIT -- The feeling late on Thanksgiving Day was familiar for Caleb Williams . Down three with the game on the line and the Chicago Bears ' first division win within reach, Williams turned his most trusted weapon to pull off a come-from-behind victory against the Detroit Lions , sending the Bears home from their trip to Ford Field with a 39-35 win . Facing third-and-goal with nine seconds remaining, Williams found Rome Odunze sprinting towards the back right corner of the end zone. The route that the former 2024 first-round picks repped with the clock winding down countless times in practice was moments from paying off when Williams zipped a pass in Odunze's direction. Using every inch of his 6-foot-3 frame, Odunze leapt up in the air to grab the ball with both hands as Lions cornerback Rock Ya-Sin attempted to push the receiver out of bounds. Odunze immediately believed his feet were in bounds, given where they landed in relation to the boundary, but his 6-yard touchdown catch was briefly reviewed before being confirmed. "Obviously the camera's going to tell," Odunze said. "The eye in the sky never lies, but they were looking if I stepped out of bounds before I caught it. So thankfully I had clean toes." Not far from where Williams and Odunze walked the stage two years ago as the Bears drafted them No. 1 and No. 9 overall, respectively, the teammates enjoyed a full-circle moment as they leaned on their chemistry trust to secure Chicago's ninth win of the season. "He was brought in with me," Williams said. "So, we've been through ups, we've been through downs, we've been all of the above. And so, when those moments come up and he runs great routes, I give him the ball, he catches it. He tends to show up in those big moments. And I know he's working his tail off to be as consistent as possible each week to be able to get the ball in his hands as much as possible. We're working on that, Coach [Ben Johnson] and I. "When these big moments come up, it just tends to go to Rome." The Bears entered Week 12 riding a five-game win streak where they never trailed despite bumpy outings from the offense. It was a different story in Detroit when Chicago trailed for 53 minutes, 31 seconds of game time, only holding a lead for the final three seconds after Odunze's second of two touchdown catches gave the Bears' their latest go-ahead touchdown in a Thanksgiving game since at least the 1970 merger, according to ESPN Research. "We talk about defending every blade of grass and a game of inches and all that," Johnson said. "We talk about that every week, almost, in the building, and just a good example of that, just toe tap, right in the corner. Rome was the guy we didn't feel like we got involved enough in the first half, and so to see him come through for us in the clutch like that was awesome." Odunze's emphatic finish came after a slow start where he caught one pass for nine yards through the first three quarters. That changed in the fourth quarter as the Bears worked to erase a double-digit lead after Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs ripped off a 70-yard touchdown. All it took was three plays on Chicago's ensuing drive to find the end zone, with Williams connecting with Luther Burden for 15 yards before back-to-back throws to Odunze, with the second resulting in a 41-yard touchdown to cut the Lions' lead to 35-32. "I've learned this over my career so far," Williams said. "Yes, you go through reads, and he [Odunze] ran a great route. He did everything right. Held my eyes down the middle, took the right drop, O-line blocked well, running back, all of that. But late in games, you go to matchups. Late in games, you go to your guys. And I think that was just one of those moments that I felt good. I told Rome that I was going to keep coming back to him. "I end up missing him early in the game or earlier in the game. I ended up checking it down to [tight end] Sam [Roush] , but I told Rome I'd come back to him and having that faith, having that belief in each other and it showed up in big moments today." Odunze totaled five catches for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the fourth quarter, becoming the first Bears player with two receiving touchdowns in the final frame of a game since Brandon Marshall in 2014. The postgame locker room environment was a stark contrast to the last time Williams, Odunze and many other Bears were in Detroit for a Thanksgiving game. In 2024, the Bears let the clock run out without using their final timeout against the Lions as Williams put his team in position for a comeback win. Former Bears coach Matt Eberflus was fired one day later. Two years removed from that low point, linebackers Devin Bush and D'Marco Jackson lifted Johnson onto their shoulders and paraded him in celebration as their teammates yelled and cheered. Williams, who took a hit to his midsection late in the game, was getting an X-ray during the postgame festivities, which had settled down by the time he got back. He said it was nothing more than a bruise. Odunze's performance earned him his first game ball of the season. After thanking his coaches and teammates, the receiver had one of his own to give to his head coach, who Odunze said "got his get back" in his first win against the Lions. Johnson served as Detroit's offensive coordinator from 2022-24 and was 0-2 against his former team as a head coach. His first win against the Lions earned the Bears a critical head-to-head tiebreaker over a Detroit team they will host in Week 17 along with sole possession of first place in the NFC North. "They had what we wanted, and for us, we wanted to go take it," Johnson said. "It was a big game for them, big game for us, and we knew it was going to be a slug fight, just like it was. It was a lot of back-and-forth, there were a lot of fireworks scored throughout that game. And like I said, I think going into this, one of those things -- it could come down to, whoever has the ball last could end up being the team that wins this one. So again, I think those guys played really hard throughout, and a ton of respect for Detroit."

stories.title: Dez Bryant goes off on Cowboys in NSFW rant after implosion vs. Eagles: ‘Get everybody the f–k out’
stories.summary: Dez Bryant didn’t hold back after watching his former Cowboys team author that largest Thanksgiving collapse in NFL history.
stories.detailText: Dez Bryant didn’t hold back after watching his former Cowboys team author the largest Thanksgiving collapse in NFL history. The legendary wide receiver, who was in attendance in Texas, was calling for Cowboys owner Jerry Jones to clean house as the team was in the process of blowing a 21-point third-quarter lead with a calamity of a fourth quarter. Bryant doubled down after Jake Elliott’s 59-yard field goal with three seconds remaining gave the Eagles an improbable 39-38 win at AT&T Stadium on Thursday. Dez Bryant Getty Images for Fanatics Sports “Jerry, Jerry, Jerry, everybody got to get the f–k up out of here,” Bryant, who played eight years on Dallas from 2010-2017, said in a video posted to social media . “F–k that. That’s completely unacceptable. That is unacceptable. F–k that “Get everybody the f–k up out of here. Fire everybody. Fire’m all. F–k it. Fire’m, get everybody the f–k out. F–k that. Fire everybody.” The Cowboys were as much to blame for losing the game as the Eagles were for winning, as they surrendered a blocked punt for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter, watched usually automatic kicker Brandon Aubrey miss from 40 yards on a kick that would have given them a five-point lead with 3:27 remaining in the game. Dallas (5-7) chose to try to put the game away by going for it on fourth and 1 from the Eagles’ 41, but Dak Prescott was sacked, setting up Philly’s last-gasp effort. Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer speaks at a press conference after the Cowboys’ 39-38 stunning loss to the Eagles on Nov. 26, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. AP Photo/Sam Hodde The loss denied the Cowboys a chance to get to .500 and keep themselves in the thick of the NFC East race, which should put coach Brian Schottenheimer further on the hot seat. Jones called the loss a “bitter disappointment” to reporters. He said that a coaching change is “not a thought on my mind at this particular time” and that there are “several more games to go and we have to have our mind on that.” Dallas owner Jerry Jones speaks to the media after the Cowboys’ stunning Thanksgiving loss to the Eagles. AP Photo/Sam Hodde Former Cowboys QB Joe Milton threw for 331 yards, two touchdowns and one interception for the Eagles (4-7), who kept their slim playoff hopes alive. DeVonta Smith caught 11 passes for 200 yards and two scores as the Dallas defense continues to struggle.

stories.title: Schottenheimer defends 4th-down call before Eagles' 59-yard FG in 39-38 stunner over Cowboys
stories.summary: — Brian Schottenheimer said he second-guesses plenty of his decisions, just not the one that will be dissected more than any other in his two seasons as coach of the Dallas Cowboys.
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Brian Schottenheimer said he second-guesses plenty of his decisions, just not the one that will be dissected more than any other in his two seasons as coach of the Dallas Cowboys . Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field with 2 seconds remaining, and the Philadelphia Eagles stunned the Cowboys by rallying for a 39-38 Thanksgiving victory on Thursday. The Eagles (4-7) got a chance for the win when Schottenheimer decided to go for it with a two-point lead on fourth-and-1 from the Philadelphia 39-yard line with 55 seconds remaining. Dak Prescott was sacked at the 48 of the Eagles, who needed just 11 yards to give Elliott a shot at the long field goal with 7 seconds to go. A punt could have run off about 10 seconds and pinned the Eagles deep in their end of the field with no timeouts. The shocking loss is sure to turn up the pressure on Schottenheimer after the Cowboys (5-7) again failed to win consecutive games and made any path to the playoffs difficult at best. “Absolutely not in that situation,” Schottenheimer said when asked if he second-guessed the decision. “There's things that come up and you look at the film and you want to know, ‘What do you think about that?’ But that situation, absolutely not.” The Cowboys have one of the worst defenses in the league, and let Joe Milton , a quarterback who couldn't win the backup job behind Prescott in training camp this year, throw for 331 yards in just his third career start. All three have been with the Eagles since he was signed off the Dallas practice squad last month. Prescott is taking his responsibility, saying he didn't communicate a change at the line of scrimmage and then hesitated on a throw to CeeDee Lamb before Ty Robinson closed in for the sack. “That's one I'll think about for a long time,” Prescott said. “Still had a chance at the throw, just so the DB was playing CeeDee pretty physical. And then I couldn’t get off of that, felt the pressure, and took the sack. And I can’t do that. Most important part of the game.” Dallas' only winning streak in two seasons with Schottenheimer was a three-game run last November capped by a Thanksgiving win over Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City. The Cowboys led by 21 points in the third quarter — the biggest blown lead in Thanksgiving history — and were still up 14 in the fourth before the Eagles started their improbable comeback by blocking a punt and returning it for a touchdown. Milton had touchdown passes of 50 and 45 yards to DeVonta Smith and a 14-yard scoring run as the Eagles won when they were already missing quarterback Jalen Hurts and lost star running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) and cornerback Cooper DeJean (concussion) in the first quarter. The defending NFC East champions have won back-to-back games since a seven-game losing streak. “A lot of emotions, but mainly just so happy for this team,” said Milton, who was Prescott's backup last year before losing the job to Sam Howell this preseason. “This team never let up. These guys on the sideline, they never dropped their head. Everybody just kept saying, ‘We’re good, we’re good. We’re gonna keep going.'” Prescott threw for two touchdowns and ran for a score while Javonte Williams accounted for three TDs in a game the Cowboys didn’t trail until Elliott’s winning kick. The Cowboys were up 14 early in the fourth when Robinson blocked Bryan Anger’s punt, and Kenny Moore II picked up the bouncing ball at the Dallas 3 for the easy score. Prescott answered by running through and vaulting over Moore on a 14-yard run that restored the two-touchdown lead. Dallas then had another special teams breakdown on Britain Covey 's 55-yard kickoff return. Smith, who finished with a career-high 200 yards receiving, had a 23-yard catch after having gone to the sideline earlier with an apparent back injury when he landed hard on an incompletion. Milton ran 15 yards for a score on the next play. The Eagles went for a 2-point conversion and didn't get it, so they had to try again after Makai Lemon 's 24-yard TD catch pulled them within 38-36 with 2:10 remaining. After a holding penalty, Milton's pass was broken up at the goal line. Before Lemon's score, Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal that would have put Dallas up 11. Milton was 21 of 31 for 331 yards with three touchdowns in his third career start. The 50-yarder to Smith marked the fifth consecutive week the Dallas defense has given up a touchdown at least that long. Prescott's scoring passes were to KaVontae Turpin and Williams, who also had scoring runs of 1 and 12 yards. Lamb had seven catches for 134 yards for Dallas. The Cowboys have lost to backup quarterbacks at home three times this season. One of them was Arizona, when Dallas matched a franchise record by blowing a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter in a 33-30 overtime loss. This time, the Cowboys let the Eagles match the biggest fourth-quarter comeback on Thanksgiving at 14 points. Chicago beat Detroit 23-17 in overtime in 1980. “I guess I said a couple of weeks ago after the Arizona game how stunning that one was,” Prescott said. “But this definitely takes the cake.” Injuries Eagles: TE Dallas Goedert didn’t return after injuring a shoulder in the first quarter. Cowboys: DT Quinnen Williams injured his back in the fourth quarter. Up next Eagles: At Arizona on Dec. 6. Cowboys: At Seattle on Dec. 7. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Brady disappointed in Rodgers' McCarthy comments: 'Nobody wins'
stories.summary: Tom Brady expressed his disappointment in how Aaron Rodgers handled his exit from Pittsburgh, saying there are things in the locker room that shouldn't be made public.
stories.detailText: Tom Brady expressed his disappointment in how fellow future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers handled his benching and exit from the Pittsburgh Steelers , saying "nobody wins when the family feuds." Brady addressed the situation during the Fox broadcast of Eagles-Cowboys on Thursday, one day after Rodgers went scorched earth on Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy in a lengthy interview on "The Pat McAfee Show." "[The] NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we shouldn't ever lose track of that as players," Brady said. "It's a privilege to be in that locker room, when you're fighting with your teammates, you're fighting with your coaches, you're always acting as a team together. It shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public, that's what I'll say." Following the news of his benching for backup Mason Rudolph , Rodgers went after McCarthy with a litany of accusations -- including that the coach has slept through team meetings -- and called into question his fitness to coach. Brady called Rodgers a "tremendous player" but said the situation he created was "unfortunate." A seven-time Super Bowl champion, Brady reflected that it's his relationships with his coaches and teammates that he cherishes most from his Hall of Fame career. "I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years, and what made a great teammate to me was, you cared about your teammates and your coaches and you cared about what the team was trying to accomplish," he said. "And that supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote. "I was in a great locker room. I played for my teammates, I played for my coaches ... nobody wins when the family feuds." As for where the Steelers go from here -- team owner Art Rooney II has already backed McCarthy as coach -- Brady said the hope is they regroup ahead of Friday afternoon's game against the Denver Broncos . "And all those teammates have to -- they're going to go and regroup and that's going to hopefully galvanize them toward, you know you feel like you're in the foxhole together," Brady said.

stories.title: Eagles vs. Cowboys Thanksgiving: The good, the bad, and the ugly
stories.summary: Highlights and lowlights from Philadelphia’s Week 12 win!
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, TEXAS- NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nick Sirianni had to be redirected away from the stands more than a few times by the Eagles’ media relations team at AT&T Stadium. He tried to high five everyone wearing midnight green Thursday afternoon. The Eagles were dead two times, three times, 10 times, it seemed, and they managed to stage the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history, overcoming a 21-point deficit (31–10) to beat the Dallas Cowboys, 39-38, in one of the most improbable victories games in Eagles’ memory. It sets the Eagles up to now become NFC East contenders, considered where the Eagles were two weeks ago. Credit has to go to Sirianni. The Eagles never gave up. They were banged up, without Cooper DeJean, Dallas Goedert, relying on Ty Robinson’s blocked punt, and pivotal nine-yard sack that turned the ball over and set up Jake Elliott’s game-winning 59-yard field goal with 2 seconds left. But the game belonged to Joe Milton . The pickup from the Cowboys’ practice squad hauled the Eagles from a 31-10 deficit to complete 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards and three touchdowns being named MVP of the game. DeVonta Smith was amazing in a career-high game, catching a career-high 11 passes for a career-high 200 yards on 14 targets. It is a signature victory in Sirianni’s six years. Elliott is The Eagles are now 4-7 with the lowly Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts next, two teams with a combined 6-16 record, which could bring the Eagles to 6-7 record with Seattle coming to Lincoln Financial Field on Dec. 19. The Eagles are still at the bottom of the NFC East, but in a position to push the 6-3-1 New York Giants, and the 4-5-1 Washington Commanders. The Eagles’ 20 fourth-quarter points exceeded the 17-points per game the Eagles were averaging this season. The Eagles continued playing hard for Sirianni. He still made dubious choices, like the decision to go for a two-point conversion after Milton’s 15-yard TD run with 9:09 left to play, and the Eagles trailing 38-30. It does not matter now—the Eagles won. The Eagles were down at one point 31-10 with 3:35 left in the third quarter, then proceeded to score on four of the next five drives. There was a lot of good, some bad and some ugly in the Eagles’ 39-38 win over the Dallas Cowboys. The Good Joe Milton exploding on national TV in completing 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards and three touchdowns. He just had a habit of coming up in clutch situations to make big plays. He probably made himself a pile of money from some NFL team, too, whether the Eagles are in his future or somewhere else. Wherever he goes, no Eagles’ fan will forget what he did on Thanksgiving Day 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys, bringing a dead team back to life. Ty Robinson’s blocked punt and Kenny Moore’s 3-yard scoop and score suddenly made what looked like a blowout into a game. Robinson came slicing through the line and dove at Dallas punter Bryan Anger to catch the punt with his right hand, and Moore ran after the loose ball and gathered it in for a three-yard score. Robinson later came up with a huge nine-yard sack at the Eagles’ 48 with 55 seconds left, setting up the Elliott game-winner. Jake Elliott coming through big again. He was 2-for-2 on a 48- and 59-yard game-winning field goal. This came after Elliott went 4-for-4 the previous week against Pittsburgh with field goals of 41, 29, 53 and 55 yards. Elliott is 13 of 14 on field goal attempts, and 21 of 21 on extra points—including 5-for-5 on field goals attempts of 50 yards or more. Sirianni is going to have to think more of Elliott kicking field goals instead of trying to go for it on fourth down. What sometimes gets lost is Elliott is a two-time Super Bowl champion who has made huge field goals in huge games. DeVonta Smith seemed to be the only weapon the Eagles had, and despite added attention, he caught a game-high 11 passes for a game-high 200 yards on 14 targets, including 50- and 45-yard touchdown catches. It was Smith’s 45-yard TD catch with 15 seconds left in the third quarter that continued to make the game intriguing pulling the Eagles within 31-17. Milton’s 50-yard rainbow to DeVonta Smith for the Eagles’ only touchdown in the first half. Milton was about the only thing the Eagles had going in the first half. Otherwise, it was bad. Two of Milton’s first three passes converted third downs. They were the first two good signs the Eagles might be able to move the ball against the NFL’s 31st defense. Milton’s first completion was a nine-yard completion to Dallas Goedert on a second-and-eight to the Eagles’ 17. Three plays later. Milton connected with Smith for a 16-yard reception to the Eagles’ 35. Of course, the Eagles blew it by going for it on fourth-and-one at the Dallas 37. Money on third down. Milton completed eight of his first 11 passes, three of which came on third down. On the Eagles’ first drive, he hit Smith for 16 yards on a third-and-8, and on third drive, he hit Makai Lemon for 20-yard pass on a third-and-12 to the Dallas 34. It led to Elliott’s 48-yard field goal. Byron Young with nine tackles from the defensive tackle position. He had five solo tackles, assisting on four. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. continues to lead the defense. Every time the linebacker out of St, Joe’s Prep and Clemson has started this season, he has led the Eagles in tackles. Thanksgiving against Dallas was no different, with a game-high 12 tackles, seven solo, with a sack and two tackles for loss. Trotter is now second on the Eagles in tackles with 64 tackles, although has a team-high 41 solo tackles. The Bad Cobie Durant’s interception with 7:05 to play seemed to seal the victory for the Cowboys after the Eagles’ fourth stop of the game. Brandon Aubrey missed a gimme 40-yard field goal attempt bailed out the Eagles. The Eagles losing Cooper DeJean, Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert to injury in the first quarter. Not that it mattered. The Ugly Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell flagged with pass interference on the very first play of the game. The 17-yard call took the ball from the Dallas 23 to the Cowboys’ 40 and jumpstarted one of the NFL’s most potent offenses. Mitchell was called for two pass interferences penalties for a total of 46 yards. It was not a good game for Mitchell, who was later burned for a 39-yard completion on a second-and-16 right after the Eagles’ blocked punt score. The quick euphoria the Eagles had after the blocked punt was quickly zapped on a Dak Prescott 14-yard touchdown scramble with 10:11 to play. The Eagles first half. Everyone may have given up by then and began eating their Thanksgiving Day dinner. The Cowboys scored on four of their first five drives. They had outgained the Eagles, 245 to 169, had 17 first downs to the Eagles’ eight, and the Eagles committed penalties for 71 yards, including Quinyon Mitchell’s second interference call for 29 yards, and Riq Woolen’s 10-yard interference call leading to the Cowboys’ last touchdown in the first half. The Cowboys converted 6 of 7 third downs to the Eagles’ 2 of 5. With 5:09 left in the first half, the Cowboys scored on three of their four possessions, had amassed 208 total yards of offense, averaging 8.3 yards a play, 12.9 yards a pass and 5.3 yards a rush. Zak Prescott was 6 of 10 for 129 yards and a touchdown. Dak Prescott’s 31-yard touchdown pass to Kavontae Turpin for a Cowboys’ 14-0 lead with 36 seconds left in the first quarter. It looked like the route was on. The Cowboys’ second drive. This time,the Cowboys needed just five plays to score. But they came up with a big third-down play again, this time, on a third-and-16, when Prescott hit George Pickens for a 36-yard completion to the Eagles’ 33. Riq Woolen made the tackle, and earned a benching again, but the Eagles were so depleted, they had to keep the problem on the field. Sirianni opting to go for it on fourth-and-one at the Cowboys’ 36, passing on a 53-yard field attempt by Elliott. Will Shipley caught jawing on the sideline with Nick Sirianni in the first quarter, no doubt about playing time. The Cowboys’ first drive of the game. It was an 11-play, 77-yard drive that chewed up 6 minutes and 11 seconds off the clock. Of the Cowboys’ 11 plays, they only faced three third downs—converting all of them. The true backbreaker was Prescott’s 28-yard completion to CeeDee Lamb right down the middle of the field to the Eagles’ 7. Three plays later, Javonte Williams scored from a yard out for a 7-0 Dallas lead with 8:50 to play in the first quarter. Of the Cowboys’ first 11 plays, they threw it only three times, while Williams gashed them for 35 yards. It was the ghost of the previous Dallas game, when Williams sliced his way through the Eagles for 155 yards rushing, averaging 6.2 yards a carry. In the first game, the Cowboys ran 65 plays against the Eagles’ defense for zero tackles for a loss. Dallas pounded the Eagles for 416 total yards, averaging 6.4 yards a game, with 204 yards on the ground, averaging 5.4 yards a carry. The Cowboys’ first drive seemed to give loud warnings for another long day for the Eagles’ defense. There is a reason why Jihaad Campbell has struggled, it’s because he gets lost in coverage. The linebacker once again managed to lose CeeDee Lamb on a third-and-18 on the Cowboys’ first drive to the Eagles’ 7. Campbell thought he was reading Prescott’s eyes while Lamb ran right past him. It led to the first score of the game.

stories.title: Mike Tomlin on the Rodgers-McCarthy situation in Pittsburgh: 'It's a dumpster fire'
stories.summary: Tomlin addressed the Rodgers-McCarthy situation in an interview that aired during halftime of the Chiefs-Bills game.
stories.detailText: Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin sat down with Mike Tirico to discuss his reaction to everything Aaron Rodgers said in a rant during Wednesday’s episode of the “Pat McAfee Show.” The highlight of the interview was Tomlin's response when asked about his emotions watching what is happening with the Steelers after coaching them for two decades. “I'm upset about it. It's a dumpster fire and I don't say that in a judgmental way. I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years, but it certainly is upsetting and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset.” Tomlin started the interview by being asked for his general reaction to what was said. “I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday. The prevailing one is general sadness. Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback, Aaron Rogers, and just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.” The former Steelers head coach said that he was “shocked” at how the team’s dirty laundry was aired. “It certainly did. And particularly because I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years and have known and competed against Mike and respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time.” Tomlin was asked his opinion on whether or not this will impact McCarthy’s ability to continue to lead the Steelers. “It certainly created some challenges and challenges is an understatement if those thigns are true. but his ability or inability to overcome that is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys buy into what he's selling. certainly he's been there a short period of time so certainly you wonder the level of that challenge. Certainly it is relationship-based." On Tuesday night after 11 p.m. ET, it was announced that Aaron Rodgers would be inactive for the Pittsburgh Steelers’ Friday game against the Denver Broncos, and that Mason Rudolph would start. The next day, Rodgers went on “The Pat McAfee Show” and went scorched-earth on head coach Mike McCarthy, accusing him of sleeping during meetings, not watching film, and using the wrong team name during a breakdown of a team huddle. The rant sent the football world into a frenzy as local reporters confirmed anonymous sources saying it was all true, and former players and coaches, current analysts , NFL insiders, and an NFL owner came out in support of McCarthy. Tomlin was the head coach of the Steelers from 2007 to 2025. He infamously never had a losing season, but also hadn’t made the Super Bowl since 2008. At the end of the 2025 season, Rodgers’ first year with the franchise, Tomlin resigned as head coach, triggering a coaching search that ended with McCarthy's hiring.

stories.title: Mike Tomlin on current Steelers situation: "It's a dumpster fire"
stories.summary: Former Steelers coach speaks at length about this week's events.
stories.detailText: Many folks in and around football have had opinions about the recent brouhaha between former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. Few have the insight and perspective that former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin brings to the table. Appearing on NBC's Chiefs-Bills halftime show on Thanksgiving night, Tomlin shared his thoughts on the situation in a conversation with Mike Tirico. (A portion of it was on the live broadcast; the full interview is here .) "I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday," Tomlin told Tirico. "I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad on a micro level, sad on a macro level. And by that, I mean, you know, just from an individual perspective, sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum. "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football. So, just a lot of emotions, but probably more than anything, man, general sadness on a lot of levels." Tirico asked Tomlin if he was shocked by Rodgers's decision to air dirty laundry in a public forum. "It certainly did," Tomlin said, "but, you know, and particularly because I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years, and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time. But I don't — what I acknowledge is I don't know them as a collective, the nature of their relationships, and so certainly I was surprised by that." Regardless of Rodgers's conduct on the way out the door, Tomlin explained that Rodgers was viewed favorably by his teammates in 2025. "He was beloved, and I'm not, you know, over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real, natural way. He was a tireless worker regarding the process. "I called early-morning quarterback meetings on Wednesday and Thursday. He was always early and engaged. Did a heck of a job in terms of engaging and developing, assisting in the development of young players. Specifically, Will Howard was always in that meeting, and, shoot, man, [Rodgers] and I were shoulder-to-shoulder in terms of the development of Will and challenging Will to develop professional habits. And so, you know, it was early and extremely consistent during my time with him, in terms of his willingness to work in those areas, and I think that's why he's so beloved in that locker room, as been reported by multiple sources in light of this incident. That is real. The guys in that locker room love and appreciate Aaron Rodgers." Had Tomlin gotten any sense that things were so close to breaking down? "Absolutely none, but it's a really specific reason why, to be honest with you, man," Tomlin said. "One of my cultural mantras, when I worked there for the 19 years, is don't talk to people about your problems unless they can be a component of the solution. Because if you do, it's counterproductive, and people know where I stand there. And by that I mean if you have a problem with your playing time, don't talk to your teammate about it. Talk to somebody that can do something about it. That's problem solving. "And so everybody understands my posture on some of that stuff, and so although I have really good, fluid communication with many of those guys, particularly, the more veteran guys, they know me and know me well enough to know that I didn't want to hear about any potential issues, because I'm not a component of the solution. And so although, particularly, like, Cam Heyward, he and I spent a little time together doing his bye week. Man, we had no mention of anything bubbling under the surface, if you will." Can McCarthy effectively lead the team, given what Rodgers said? "You know, it certainly created some challenges and challenges is probably an understatement if all of those things are true," Tomlin told Tirico. "And certainly the '1-2-3 Packers' is, because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him, or how those guys buy into what he's selling. And so, certainly, he's been there a short period of time. And so it makes you wonder, the level of that challenge. But it'll be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned." How does Tomlin think the Steelers will fare against the Broncos on Friday? "Based on my knowledge of the men, particularly the leaders, the longstanding guys, they'll do a great job of getting hyper-focused on what really matters, and that's that football game," Tomlin said. "They'll use it as a mantra to bring them together. I expect those guys to fight. Now, fight and quality play are two different things. I'm certainly not gonna expect those guys not to fight. I think they're gonna fight and fight extremely hard. What I'm interested in is quality of play, quality of execution. And those are things that could be impacted by the level of distraction that they had on a short week in particular." Tirico then asked Tomlin how he feels, overall, about what has transpired this week. "I'm upset about it, you know, it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgmental way. I presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset." If owner Art Rooney II calls Tomlin for advice, what would Tomlin say? "Hey, Mike, that's a hypothetical, because I know he wouldn't and, and because I know how he's trained," Tomlin said. "You know, Art is a guy that's not a hedge fund guy that bought a football team. He's not a, you know, artificial intelligence guy that bought a football team. This is a family business. It's generational. Any advice or thought process in that way, I imagine he just says, 'What would my dad do?' Or, 'What would my grandfather do?' Their mode of operation is time tested, it's generational. And so, I doubt, very, very seriously, that he called anyone for outside advice." Finally, Tirico asked whether Tomlin believes Rodgers will get another NFL opportunity this season, if he wants one. "There's certainly a possibility for that," Tomlin said. "And I just say that based on the 19 years that I held the position that I held. It's a 32-team league. All it takes is one. Over time, I've laughed and watched that people talk about, you know, 'No, that could never happen.' In a 32-team league, when everybody is highly competitive and there's some real challenges, particularly as you get to this portion of the journey from a player availability standpoint, there's certainly a possibility if he desires that he could play again, because all it takes is one suitor." Having cleared waivers, Rodgers is available to that one suitor, if/when that one suitor calls. Still, that one suitor will need to be willing to accept the risk that, if Rodgers doesn't have things go the way he wants, he'll choose to do again the same thing he did this week.

stories.title: Eagles' Nick Sirianni pulled away from fans after wild Thanksgiving win over Cowboys
stories.summary: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni ran over to the high-end AT&T Stadium suites after his team beat the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving.
stories.detailText: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has been known to lose his cool on sidelines before. A dramatic 39-38 come-from-behind Thanksgiving Day victory over the rival Dallas Cowboys, punctuated by a 60-yard field goal from Jake Elliott with 2 seconds remaining, was certainly cause for celebration. Sirianni needed to meet Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer for the customary postgame handshake between the two head coaches, but instead ran toward a smattering of fans in the first-row luxury seating at AT&T Stadium, including several Cowboys fans, to celebrate. Sirianni was pulled away by Eagles' security chief Dom DiSandro, with senior vice president for communications Bob Lange in tow. THE LARGEST COMEBACK ON THANKSGIVING EVER!! 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/lQa0X9THci — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 27, 2026 The Eagles trailed 31-10 late in the third quarter before erasing the deficit, with former Cowboys backup quarterback Joe Milton (eventually named the game's MVP) leading the way. Sirianni's postgame meeting with Schottenheimer was brief. Walking in the tunnel afterward, Sirianni let out a triumphant yell. "That's how you fight," he said. "We know how to fight." Nick Sirianni fired up after that win. pic.twitter.com/fAbwKLZo70 — Dave Zangaro (@DZangaroNBCS) November 27, 2026 This is not the first time Sirianni has acted oddly with regard to fans. Earlier this month, he had to deny flipping off home fans as the team dropped to 2-7. He had to apologize in 2024 for engaging with fans negatively despite a win at home. Earlier in the game, running back Will Shipley and Sirianni got into it on the sidelines. Other antics of Sirianni's have included staring down the camera and running toward the end zone to celebrate with his players after a touchdown. He led the Eagles to the Super Bowl 59 title and the team has made the playoffs every season he has been the head coach. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Eagles' Nick Sirianni pulled away from fans after wild Thanksgiving win over Cowboys

stories.title: Steelers owner Art Rooney II 'disappointed' in Rodgers outcome, backs McCarthy
stories.summary: Steelers owner Art Rooney II reacted to Wednesday's fiery interview from Aaron Rodgers by saying he was "disappointed in where this went" with their now-former quarterback, adding he has "100% confidence in Mike McCarthy."
stories.detailText: PITTSBURGH -- A day after Aaron Rodgers unleashed a firestorm of accusations about Mike McCarthy's fitness to coach, Pittsburgh Steelers owner and president Art Rooney II said in a statement to ESPN on Thursday that he has "100% confidence in Mike McCarthy" while also telling a newspaper that he supported moving on from Rodgers. Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette that "insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that." The stunning decision to bench and release Rodgers was prompted in part by the quarterback's demands to make changes to the playcalling structure. Rooney told the Post-Gazette that he "expects" McCarthy to "be our coach this season, next season and beyond." He reiterated that sentiment to ESPN. "I am disappointed in where this went with Aaron Rodgers, but I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy," Rooney said in his statement. "And I have tremendous confidence in Mason Rudolph and the other players in our locker room. "Decisions were made on what we believe is in the best interest of the Pittsburgh Steelers. Our main focus right now is preparing for tomorrow's game." Rodgers made a litany of accusations in a 34-minute interview on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday that included McCarthy sleeping in meetings, missing meetings and breaking down a huddle at halftime of last week's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles with "1, 2, 3, Packers " -- an incident McCarthy said was an "embarrassing moment." Rooney told the Post-Gazette he doesn't have any concerns about McCarthy's health. "Mike's as healthy as the rest of us," Rooney said. "Health was not an issue. I'm not sure where that part comes." In Wednesday's interview, Rodgers said he found out from teammate Pat Freiermuth that he was being benched in favor of Rudolph and would be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos and hadn't heard the news from McCarthy. McCarthy responded to the allegations when he met with the media later Wednesday, saying the Steelers front office was "very in tune with everything that goes on in football operations as far as my job responsibility." Rooney said in his statement to ESPN that he has "responsibility for ensuring the team and entire organization meets our standards." The Steelers waived Rodgers shortly after the interview Wednesday. He officially cleared waivers Thursday , making him a free agent.

stories.title: Jeffery Simmons: I didn't simulate snap count on false starts, Lions are "crying" about a them problem
stories.summary: Long before the Bears beat the Lions on a last-second touchdown catch by wide receiver Rome Odunze, one of the storylines of the game was a run of false start penalties by the Lions.
stories.detailText: Long before the Bears beat the Lions on a last-second touchdown catch by wide receiver Rome Odunze, one of the storylines of the game was a run of false start penalties by the Lions. Center Juice Scruggs was called for back-to-back false starts and then picked up a third later in the half. Left guard Christian Mahogany was flagged for another one before the next snap and there were indications from the Lions that Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was simulating the snap count to get them to jump. Mahogany made that accusation explicit after the game that the Bears "find out the snap count of the quarterback and they use it" while adding that Lions linemen were wearing microphones that he believes will back him up. Simmons was not penalized, but was seen speaking to the referee during a break in play. He denied Mahogany's allegation after the 39-35 win. "We don’t have to . We don't have to," Simmons said, via Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press "We line up and play football. They quarterback check. I said, 'Run.' I didn't say, 'Hut.' I mean, their cadence, they say, 'White 80, white 80.' I mean, when you lose football games, it's a lot of complaining and a lot of crying. I mean, there was a couple times that they false start, we didn't say a word. So that's their problem, not ours. . . . If I say, 'Run,' I'm telling my defense, run. Think I care to tell them what they about to do? I'm talking to my guys. So all the crying that they're doing, that's a them problem, not me." Mahogany was flagged for taunting Simmons during a 70-yard Jahmyr Gibbs touchdown run in the fourth quarter and kicker Jake Bates missed the ensuing extra point to leave the score 35-24. The Lions would not score again and the Bears headed back to Chicago with an improbable victory.

stories.title: Joe Milton has huge game as Eagles shock Cowboys
stories.summary: Dallas blew a 21-point lead as Philly made a spectacular comeback with Milton at the helm.
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, Texas -- Quarterback Joe Milton shined on the national stage, helping erase a 21-point third-quarter deficit to lead the Philadelphia Eagles to a thrilling 39-38 shootout win over the Dallas Cowboys to keep some hope alive in what's been a trying season. Milton accounted for four touchdowns (three passing, one rushing) and made a number of "wow" throws with his howitzer arm, the bulk of which went to receiver DeVonta Smith , who erupted for 186 receiving yards and two scores. Milton did enough in the closing moments to set up a game-winning 59-yard field goal by Jake Elliott . Any progress the defense made following quality outings against the New York Giants and Pittsburgh Steelers in consecutive games was stopped cold by a Dallas attack that was a clear step up in weight class, but the Eagles firmed up late to give Philly a chance. Injuries hit, as they have all season, with running back Saquon Barkley (stinger), defensive back Cooper DeJean (concussion), tight end Dallas Goedert (shoulder), safety Marcus Epps (foot) and defensive tackle Gabe Hall (wrist) all forced to the sideline. But with a pair of gettable games coming up against the Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts , it's not inconceivable the Eagles could turn this into a four-game winning streak as they attempt to climb out of the NFC East basement. Here are the most important things to know from Thursday night for both teams: Philadelphia Eagles (4-7) What to make of the QB performance: The Eagles have something with Milton. He's shown playmaking ability in three starts since being signed off the Cowboys' practice squad last month, including a pair of long touchdown passes to Smith on Thursday. Showing off his ultra strong arm -- he wants to be called "Mr. Rocket" for a reason -- both TDs traveled 40-plus yards in the air. Jalen Hurts , who is out with blood clots, has five such TDs in his regular-season career, seven including playoffs. Philly should consider keeping Milton, who finished 21-of-31 for 331 yards, around beyond this season and continue to develop him. Trend to watch: After getting gashed for 204 rushing yards in its first matchup with Dallas, the defense yielded more than 151 yards and three touchdowns on the ground in the rematch, including three first-half rushing scores by Javonte Williams . Philadelphia has been underwhelming as a rush defense this season, entering the game ranked 20th in average yards allowed per game (120.8). Stat to know: Milton's 50-yard touchdown pass to Smith in the second quarter traveled 64.4 yards in air distance, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. It is the longest touchdown pass by an Eagles quarterback with that distance since the stat began being tracked in 2016. Packers quarterback Jordan Love 's touchdown pass to receiver Christian Watson on Oct. 11 was 66.9 yards and is the only other NFL completion this season of 64-plus yards. -- Tim McManus Next game: Dec. 6 at Arizona Cardinals Dallas Cowboys (5-7) If anything summed up the Cowboys' season, it was Thursday's loss to the Eagles. A comfortable 28-10 halftime lead disappeared. A 14-point fourth-quarter advantage vanished. The defense caved. The special teams fell apart (blocked punt returned for a touchdown, missed field goal try). They failed on a late fourth-down attempt to close the game. The offense lost its aggressiveness. And the Cowboys might have lost their hope. Joe Milton made the Cowboys look foolish for not keeping him as their No. 2 quarterback, throwing three touchdowns and running for another. As a result, the Cowboys continue to find inventive ways to not win consecutive games on the season. The Cowboys have not won consecutive contests since last year's Thanksgiving Day victory against the Kansas City Chiefs . If the Cowboys want to end their playoff drought at two seasons, they will likely need to win two of their next three games against the Seattle Seahawks , Los Angeles Rams and Jacksonville Jaguars , while sweeping their remaining two matchups against the NFC East-leading Giants and Washington Commanders . And to do that, they will somehow have to capture back-to-back games. Who knew that would be so difficult? Most surprising performance: The Cowboys special teams had been much improved in 2026, but they suffered a meltdown Thursday. A Bryan Anger punt was blocked and returned for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter. Brandon Aubrey , the highest-paid kicker in the NFL, missed a 40-yard try late in the fourth. The coverage unit couldn't get the job done. All of it contributed to one of the more humiliating losses in team history. Stat to know: Javonte Williams has done something that fellow running backs Ezekiel Elliott and Hall of Famers Emmitt Smith and Bob Hayes didn't achieve in their first two years with the Cowboys. Williams has 28 touchdowns in his first two seasons in Dallas, tied with receiver Terrell Owens (2006-07) for the most in Cowboys history. Elliott (2016-17) and Hayes (1965-66) had 25 in their first two years, while Smith (1990-91) had 24 in his first two. Trend to watch: Maybe it should be expected by now. The Cowboys gave up another play of at least 50 yards when Milton rolled left and threw back right for a 50-yard touchdown to receiver DeVonta Smith. It was the fifth straight game in which the Cowboys have allowed a touchdown of at least 50 yards, the longest streak since the Texans gave up five straight in Weeks 5 through 9 in 2024. It's the eighth play of at least 50 yards the Cowboys have allowed in the past five games and the 11th they have allowed on the season. -- Todd Archer Next game: Dec. 7 at Seattle Seahawks

stories.title: Tom Brady rips into Aaron Rodgers for breaking ‘the sanctity of an NFL locker room’
stories.summary: Another Hall of Fame quarterback is coming out against Aaron Rodgers' recent comments.
stories.detailText: Another Hall of Fame quarterback is coming out against Aaron Rodgers’ recent comments. This time it was Tom Brady, who kept it professional but made clear that Rodgers’ takedown of the Steelers after his benching needed to stay in house. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place,” Brady said on the Fox broadcast of the Eagles’ 39-38 win over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving in Dallas. “We shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together. Shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” Fox Sports broadcast analyst Tom Brady looks on before the 49ers’ win over the Cowboys on Nov. 15, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Steelers announced on Tuesday night that they were benching Rodgers against the Broncos in favor of Mason Rudolph, and Rodgers responded on Wednesday by going scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show.” Among Rodgers’ gripes was the 19-year coach falling asleep in team meetings and leading a “1, 2, 3, Packers” chant after a huddle. The Steelers cut Rodgers soon after the appearance on “McAfee,” and he cleared waivers Thursday to become a free agent. Brady, who knows a thing or two about working with longtime coaches, acknowledged that feuds can happen in the locker room, but that doesn’t mean things need to boil over like they did in Pittsburgh. “I wasn’t a perfect player, [Bill Belichick] wasn’t a perfect coach, but we did some things in the game that we’re so proud of now,” Brady said. “And even me being four years removed from the game, things that matter more than winning a Super Bowl or trophy is my relationship with my teammates, my coaches. That’s going to transcend anything you do on the field. “It’s just unfortunate. I hate it, I hate to be even talking about it. It’s a privilege to be in the NFL. You want to inspire the next generation of athletes, and you always want to do it the right way.” Aaron Rodgers wears a frustrated expression during the Steelers’ loss to the Eagles on Nov. 22, 2026, in Philadelphia. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brady wasn’t the only NFL legend who had something to say Thursday on Fox. Michael Strahan, Howie Long, and former Steelers quarterback Terry Bradshaw took time out of the pregame show to discuss Rodgers’ comments. While Rodgers now has the ability to sign with any team, his release by the Steelers may spell the end of his NFL career. ESPN insider Adam Schefter reported Thursday that it’s unlikely Rodgers finds a landing spot to finish out the season.

stories.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles pulled off the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history.
stories.detailText: Prior to Thursday, Thanksgiving Day had never seen what the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off, and it stunned social media. The Eagles defeated the Dallas Cowboys 39-38 , wiping away a 21-point deficit for the largest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history. According to ESPN Analytics, the Cowboys had a 99.4% chance to win after Brandon Aubrey 's field goal gave Dallas a 21-point lead with 3:35 remaining in the third quarter. Instead, Philadelphia scored a touchdown on three of its next four offensive possessions. The Eagles also returned a blocked punt for a touchdown early in the fourth quarter. Dallas missed a 40-yard field goal with 3:27 left, and Philadelphia answered with another touchdown. It missed its two-point conversion, making it a 38-36 game. The Cowboys then turned it over on downs, and Jake Elliott nailed a 59-yarder to put the Eagles up for good -- capping a remarkable comeback. The wild turn of events shocked the NFL world and beyond on social media, led by two former Eagles. Former Eagles center and Super Bowl champion Jason Kelce headlined the reaction, posting a selfie with a caption that read: "F--- YESSSSSSSS!!!!!" His former teammate, Darius Slay, also chimed in, and former Cowboy receiver Dez Bryant offered his thoughts. Even Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark reacted to the Cowboys' collapse, specifically the failed fourth-down conversion.

stories.title: Jerry Jones still confident about Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer, doesn't expect coaching change after Thanksgiving loss to Eagles
stories.summary: The Cowboys owner has fired a head coach during the season only once in his tenure.
stories.detailText: Thanksgiving wound up being a very bad night for Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, but it apparently won't cost him his job. Immediately after the Cowboys' collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday , team owner Jerry Jones told reporters he doesn't expect to make a coaching change any time soon. Instead, Jones suggested continuity would give Dallas its best chance in the coming weeks. Via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram : "I wouldn't anticipate that, no, at this juncture. We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes." The Cowboys have an upcoming bye week before facing the Los Angeles Rams on Dec. 20. Jones went on to say he was still " confident " about Schottenheimer, but made clear that confidence was based on nothing the team showed Thursday : "Nothing we've seen out here tonight, but you've got to look at everything. That's certainly not the thought on my mind at this particular time. We've got several more games to go and we've got to have our mind on that." Thanksgiving really was that bad for the Cowboys, who led 28-10 at halftime and held a lead as large as 21 points near the end of the third quarter. Brian Schottenheimer had a bad Thanksgiving. AP Photo/Sam Hodde The team was then hit with a cascading series of disasters. Former Cowboys backup Joe Milton led the Eagles to touchdowns on three of their next four drives, with the Eagles also returning a blocked punt for a touchdown. The Cowboys still had the advantage in the final minute, but decided to go for it on fourth down in Eagles territory and watched Dak Prescott get sacked. Eagles kicker Jake Elliott proceeded to make a 59-yard field goal in the final seconds. A Prescott interception ended the game. Both the overall collapse and late-game decision-making left nearly every finger in Dallas pointing at Schottenheimer, who has been facing the hot seat for some time. He said he wasn't worried about such speculation after the game, via Jon Machota of The Athletic : "I don't worry about that. I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn't affect me." Schottenheimer's hire was controversial when it was first announced, as he was hardly a popular offensive coordinator under previous head coach Mike McCarthy (who is dealing with issues of his own right now) . Jones' decision to promote Schottenheimer demanded trust in his own team's operations, and the results have been a 12-16-1 record. In more than three decades of owning the Cowboys, Jones has fired only a single head coach during the season: Wade Phillips in 2010. Jones has said he regrets that decision and that could very well be informing his thinking here, though that will hardly protect Schottenheimer in a month and a half.

stories.title: Jerry Jones backs Mike McCarthy after Aaron Rodgers' rant: 'One of the finest people around football that I've been around'
stories.summary: McCarthy coached the Cowboys from 2020 to 2024.
stories.detailText: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones offered strong praise for Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after Dallas' late loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving. McCarthy, who coached the Cowboys from 2020 to 2024, has been in the headlines this week after his former quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, leveled a series of accusations against him Wednesday on "The Pat McAfee Show." Rodgers said McCarthy slept during meetings, didn't watch film and even used the wrong team name while breaking a huddle. Since that interview aired, local beat reporters have cited anonymous sources in the building who confirmed some of the claims . While the timing likely could have been better, Jones still took the time to address the claims , and he ended up giving McCarthy his full support with effusive praise. "I offered him [McCarthy] to stay at least another year when he left. I thought he was outstanding as the head coach. Had a great command of, frankly, quarterback, offense. Can't say enough good things about him. He's, frankly, one of the finest people around football that I've been around. I can't say enough about him. I never had the type of thing that is being said about him. I never had that in consideration in any of my time with him, extending his contract, any of that it was never on the table. We never had an issue within the organization." After the 2024 season, the two sides reportedly reached an impasse in contract talks and mutually agreed to part ways. McCarthy ended his tenure in Dallas with a 49-35 record. Jones is the latest to defend McCarthy this week. Ahead of each Thanksgiving Day game, hosts on pregame shows defended the head coach and criticized how Rodgers delivered his message. Former Steelers quarterbacks Terry Bradshaw and Russell Wilson, as well as Hall of Famer Michael Strahan, were among those who spoke out against Rodgers' public delivery of criticism of McCarthy

stories.title: Cowboys turn into turkeys during epic Thanksgiving Day meltdown | Opinion
stories.summary: The Cowboys could have moved into the NFC playoff picture. Instead, a dramatic second-half collapse doomed Dallas' postseason hopes.
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, TX – Give the people what they want, Dallas Cowboys . Points. More points. Drama. And a holiday meltdown . Hail to the depleted Philadelphia Eagles , capping a wild rally with a 60-yard field goal from Jake Elliott with two seconds left that lifted them to a 39-38 victory. And shame on the Cowboys. So much shame. Again. That Dak Prescott-inspired Cowboys offense sure got off to a hot start on Turkey Day, running (and throwing) wild around the visitors, which sure kept up with recent times. The Cowboys had five possessions in the first half and scored four touchdowns. A few days earlier, when the Tennessee Titans came to town, they had eight drives and seven TDs. And the week before that, in losing a shootout against the mighty Niners, they scored touchdowns on four of the last five possessions. What an encouraging stretch during this homestand at JerryWorld. In Cowboys math, that’s 15 TDs over 18 drives in three games (until country music star Miranda Lambert’s halftime concert), which is nothing less than a certified roll. Then there’s this other Cowboys math: They are 5-7, not even a mediocre .500. And this is how their season ends. I mean, for all the feel-good flow of a 28-10 halftime lead enabled by Javonte Williams’ 3 TDs, Dallas blew it against an injury-depleted team that used Aaron Rodgers earlier in the week to snap a seven-game losing streak. Joe Milton, who was Prescott’s backup last year, heaved a 50-yard rainbow to DeVonta Smith for a touchdown in the first half to maybe wake up the people sluggish after Thanksgiving dinner. Then Milton fired a 45-yard TD strike to Smith in the second half. And that was just the beginning of the Dallas meltdown. Add a blocked punt turned into an Eagles TD, a long Philly kickoff return, a 15-yard Milton TD run and it was clear the game would not be over until it needed to be done. Like turkey time. In crunch time, Brandon Aubrey missed a field goal and the Eagles parlayed that into Milton’s fourth TD (3 passing, 1 rushing) and chance to tie the game with a two-point conversion. Whew. Reality check: The Cowboys, with all that explosive offense, still have a defense capable of imploding, of giving up huge chunks of yards, of allowing quick scores, of allowing opponents to stay in the game. Remember when they stripped first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker of his play-calling duties? They gave the reins to recently hired consultant Mike Pettine. Well, look at where that got them. So, there’s your hope, Cowboys Nation. Just don’t spend it all in one place. Dallas is out of the playoff mix for a reason. Or a few. Like those horrific losses against Arizona and Tampa Bay, and the brain lock blunders in crunch time in Rio. Good teams win those games most of the time. The Cowboys muck them up. Never mind the hope that they could ride Prescott – the quarterback passed for 11 touchdowns with just one pick, plus ran for two touchdowns on the home stand – to a remarkable rally for the playoffs. With no Eagles or Titans on the immediate horizon, it only gets worse. Next up for Dak & Company: A trip to Seattle to face the Seahawks and the NFL’s No. 1-ranked defense. After that, a trip to L.A. to face the resurging Rams and a defense finding another level with Myles Garrett back in action. Jacksonville, leading the AFC South, comes to town in December. And Dallas will have to deal with the division-leading Giants in Week 17. If it matters by then. Hope is one thing. But for the Cowboys, reality and shame are even greater in their equation. Follow Jarrett Bell on X: @JarrettBell . This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Cowboys turn into turkeys during epic Thanksgiving Day meltdown | Opinion

stories.title: Eagles-Cowboys final score: Joe Milton leads comeback victory over Dallas!
stories.summary: The Birds are 4-7!
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, TEXAS- NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles throws a pass during second half of an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images HAPPY THANKSGIVING, PHILADELPHIA EAGLES FANS! The Eagles are 4-7 after beating the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday. Final score: 39 to 38. HAHAHAHAHAHAHA. Man, I can’t believe the Eagles won that game! The Birds were looking left for dead after going down 31 to 10 with about three minutes remaining in the third quarter. Their defense was getting carved up by the Cowboys’ high-powered offense. But Joe Milton never said die! The Eagles’ quarterback led his new team to a winning effort against his former team, ultimately finishing 21/31 for 331 yards, three touchdowns, one interception, and a 121.8 passer rating. A lot of that production came through DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards (!) and two touchdowns. Ty Robinson, who blocked a punt to create an Eagles touchdown earlier in the game, came through with a much-needed fourth down sack that ultimately set up a game-winning Jake Elliott field goal! WHAT A WIN! And suddenly the Eagles’ season is not totally dead?! Could they actually win the NFC East?! Probably not … but they weren’t supposed to win this game, either! Next up for the Eagles: a road game against the Arizona Cardinals, which the Eagles will probably be favored in! Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. FIRST QUARTER The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer, per usual. The Cowboys took over at their own 23-yard line and Quinyon Mitchell was flagged for pass interference on the first snap from scrimmage. Tacky call on Q going up against George Pickens, who was also pretty handsy on that play. Facing 3rd-and-3, a quick dump off to Javonte Williams resulted in a first down. Cooper DeJean was hurt after tackling Williams. The Cowboys picked up another first down into field goal range with Andrew Mukuba missing a tackle in the hole. Facing 3rd-and-8, Dak Prescott’s first down scramble was called back by Jonathan Greenard drawing a holding penalty on Terence Steele. Facing 3rd-and-18, Prescott hit CeeDee Lamb wiiiiide open in the middle of the field for an easy first down at the seven-yard line. Great resistance there. Not! Jihaad Campbell seemed to get lost in coverage. The Cowboys then went with three straight runs to reach the end zone. 11 plays, 77 yards, 6:10 off the clock. EAGLES 0, COWBOYS 7. The Eagles started at their own 6-yard line after Britain Covey mishandled Brandon Aubrey’s bouncing kickoff. The Eagles picked up their first first down with a Joe Milton completion to Dallas Goedert. Facing 3rd-and-7 after a blitz forced a Milton incompletion, Milton ripped a nice ball to DeVonta Smith for another first down. A Cowboys player signaled incomplete, though, and Brian Schottenheimer threw his red flag to challenge the play. After commercial, it was announced that the Cowboys did not challenge in time before the Eagles got a play off. I don’t know if the review would have been conclusive enough to overturn the ruling on the field anyway. Milton hit Elijah Moore (!) in rhythm for a 25-yard completion to put the offense past midfield. Milton balling early! Facing 3rd-and-6 after two Saquon Barkley runs, Milton hit DeVonta just shy of the sticks. Facing 4th-and-short, the Eagles seemed like they might go Brotherly Shove but they instead tried a fullback dive with Barkley and it was stopped for a loss. The decision to go for it was correct. Overthought it on the play call. Just use the tush push. Disappointing end to an otherwise encouraging 11-play, 57-yard drive. The Cowboys took over at their own 37-yard line. Prescott’s deep shot to Pickens with Riq Woolen trailing bounced off of the receiver for an incompletion. Fortunate break for the Eagles’ defense. Facing 3rd-and-6, Prescott took off running for a first down but it was wiped out by another holding penalty on Javonte Williams grabbing Marcus Epps. Facing 3rd-and-16, Prescott hit Pickens for a contested grab against Woolen. Another favorable opportunity for the defense to get off the field and they just can’t do it. One play later, Prescott hit KaVontae Turpin for a 31-yard catch-and-run touchdown. Too easy. Meanwhile, Nick Sirianni was shown arguing with Will Shipley on the sideline. OK, then. EAGLES 0, COWBOYS 14. KAVONTAE TURPIN IS TOO FAST PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0MqBAQPtHh — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Nick Sirianni And Will Shipley Getting Heated On The Sideline. Saquon Barkley Was Part Of This One Too. Not Exactly A Peaceful Thanksgiving In Philly. Something Clearly Has Them All Fired Up. pic.twitter.com/pCzsNMqcnz — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 15-yard line. Milton hit Zach Ertz (!) for a catch that got wiped out with the Eagles accepting a Cowboys illegal contact penalty to end the first quarter. SECOND QUARTER Facing 3rd-and-5, Milton ran out of bounds for no gain. Three-and-out. Honestly, should’ve gone for it there, even though it was on the Eagles’ own 25-yard line. The Cowboys over at their own 35-yard line after a 24-yard punt return by Turpin. Facing 3rd-and-5 after Jihaad Campbell had good coverage on Lamb (!), Prescott hit Turpin to beat an Eagles blitz for a first down. Turpin bobbled the ball, though, and Sirianni threw his red flag to challenge the play. After review, the call was overturned and the Cowboys had to punt. Hey, a stop! If only barely. The Eagles took over at their own 18-yard line. DeVonta made a nice leaping catch against tight coverage from the Cowboys for 24 yards and a first down near midfield. Facing 3rd-and-12 after Markel Bell had a real rough rep to allow a Rashan Gary sack, Milton rolled right and hit a wide open Lemon for a first down! Milton got the juice?! Facing 3rd-and-6, Milton was blitzed and threw behind DeVonta for an incompletion. Jake Elliott came in for the 48-yard field goal make. I would’ve gone for it there, you’re not beating the Cowboys by kicking FGs. But not a bad nine-play, 52-yard drive. EAGLES 3, COWBOYS 14. The Cowboys took over at their own 40-yard line after their special teams made a smart play to draw an Eagles penalty. They picked up a first down with two runs, with Mukuba getting blocked out of the play on one. The Cowboys quickly moved into field goal range. And then into the red zone. Williams then went 12 yards easily up the gut for a touchdown. Zero resistance. EAGLES 3, COWBOYS 21. TD, Cowboys. They take a 21-3 lead. This is the second-most points the Eagles have allowed in a 1st half since Vic Fangio became the defensive coordinator. You have to go back to W4 of the 2024 season vs. TB for the last time a team scored more. That was 24 points. — Zach Berman (@ZBerm) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 30-yard line. Ertz drew a pass interference penalty to give the Eagles a first down. Milton roll left and unleashed a rocket down the field to DeVonta for a 50-yard touchdown! Hell yeah! That was fun. JOE MILTON GOES DEEP TO DEVONTA SMITH PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZcKIPvq6jS — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 JOE MILTON'S ARM TALENT IS RIDICULOUS 🎯 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2MLAir7i29 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 That Joe Milton TD throw traveled 64.4 yards in air distance, according to NextGen. It’s the longest TD throw by an Eagles QB since stat began being tracked in 2016. — Tim McManus (@Tim_McManus) November 26, 2026 The Cowboys took over at their own 29-yard line after a nice special teams tackle by Darius Cooper. stories.title: Eagles pull off miracle Thanksgiving rally as Cowboys stunningly collapse after disastrous decision
stories.summary: Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field with 2 seconds remaining, and the Philadelphia Eagles stunned the Dallas Cowboys by rallying for a 39-38 Thanksgiving victory on Thursday.
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, Texas — Jake Elliott kicked a 59-yard field with 2 seconds remaining, and the Philadelphia Eagles stunned the Dallas Cowboys by rallying for a 39-38 Thanksgiving victory on Thursday. The Eagles (4-7) got a chance for the win when Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer decided to go for it with a two-point lead on fourth-and-1 from the Philadelphia 39-yard line with 55 seconds remaining. Dak Prescott was sacked at the 48 of the Eagles, who needed just 11 yards to give Elliott a shot at the long field goal with 7 seconds to go. Philadelphia quarterback Joe Milton runs in for a touchdown during the Eagles 39-38 comeback win over the Cowboys on Nov. 26, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The shocking loss is sure to turn up the pressure on Schottenheimer after the Cowboys (5-7) again failed to win consecutive games and made any path to the playoffs difficult at best. Dallas’ only winning streak in two seasons with Schottenheimer was a three-game run last November capped by a Thanksgiving win over Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City. The Cowboys led by 21 points in the third quarter and were still up 14 in the fourth before the Eagles started their improbable comeback by blocking a punt and returning it for a touchdown. Joe Milton had touchdown passes of 50 and 45 yards to DeVonta Smith and a 14-yard scoring run against his former team as the Eagles won when they were already missing quarterback Jalen Hurts and lost star running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) and cornerback Cooper DeJean (concussion) in the first quarter. The defending NFC East champions have won back-to-back games since a seven-game losing streak. Prescott threw for two touchdowns and ran for a score while Javonte Williams accounted for three TDs in a game the Cowboys didn’t trail until Elliott’s winning kick. The Cowboys were up 14 early in the fourth when Ty Robinson blocked Bryan Anger’s punt, and Kenny Moore II picked up the bouncing ball at the Dallas 3 for the easy score. Prescott answered by running through and vaulting over Moore on a 14-yard run that restored the two-touchdown lead. Philadelphia Eagles place kicker Jake Elliott (4) celebrates after defeating the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington, Texas, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas had another special teams breakdown on Britain Covey’s 55-yard kickoff return. Smith, who finished with a career-high 200 yards receiving, had a 23-yard catch after having gone to the sideline earlier with an apparent back injury when he landed hard on an incompletion. Milton ran 15 yards for a score on the next play. The Eagles went for a 2-point conversion and didn’t get it, so they had to try again after Makai Lemon’s 24-yard TD catch pulled them within 38-36 with 2:10 remaining. After a holding penalty, Milton’s pass was broken up at the goal line. Before Lemon’s score, Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal that would have put Dallas up 11. Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Ty Robinson (95) blocks a punt by Dallas Cowboys punter Bryan Anger (5) in Arlington, Texas, Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. AP Photo/Julio Cortez The biggest mistake for Dallas belonged to Schottenheimer. The Eagles were out of timeouts when Schottenheimer tried to put the game away instead of opting for a short punt that could have pinned the Eagles deep in their end of the field. Milton, who was on Dallas’ practice squad a little more than a month ago, was 21 of 31 for 331 yards with three touchdowns in his third career start. The 50-yarder to Smith marked the fifth consecutive week the Dallas defense has given up a touchdown at least that long. Prescott’s scoring passes were to KaVontae Tuprin and Williams, who also had scoring runs of 1 and 12 yards. CeeDee Lamb had seven catches for 134 yards for Dallas.
