stories.title: Cowboys vs. Eagles recap: Dallas embarrassed by Philadelphia on Thanksgiving Day
stories.summary: The Cowboys are a national embarrassment
stories.detailText: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 26: Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys is tackled by Andrew Mukuba #24 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images It will go down in history as one of the darkest Thanksgiving Day games ever for the Dallas Cowboys. Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On the other hand it is actually very easy to fathom given everything we have seen from the Cowboys this season. They are not a good football team. They are poorly coached. They are talent-deficient. They are all of the bad things. On a day where we are supposed to be thankful it is hard to find a reason to be for this specific part of our lives. The Dallas Cowboys are a weekly embarrassment and Thursday was the latest example of it. What even happens now? First Quarter The Eagles won the toss and deferred which put the Cowboys offense to work first. Dak Prescott and the group did not waste the opportunity. Javonte Williams was served seconds, thirds, and then some as the team marched down the field, partly thanks to a huge 3rd and 18 conversion from Dak to CeeDee Lamb, but it was Williams who capped it off with the touchdown to give the home team an early 7-0 lead. JAVONTE TD pic.twitter.com/IFq12RHEEy — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Things were looking rather impressive for Joe Milton and the Eagles. I’d imagine that many Cowboys fans were starting to assume a score was happening any minute across the first drive. Thankfully that was not the case. Right around field goal range the Eagles chose to roll the dice on fourth and short… and Quinnen Williams said no! QUINNEN!!! pic.twitter.com/Yz2K1cZsqi — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Weirdly a sequence occurred on the next drive that did the first. Dak Prescott scrambled for a first on a third down, but the gain was negated by a penalty. This brought up third and long (16 here, 18 before) and Prescott connected with a star receiver (George Pickens here, CeeDee Lamb before) for the first down. After that KaVontae Turpin had a stellar catch where he turned on the boosters and reached the endzone in a flash. Dallas was up 14-0 early. TURP TD!!!! pic.twitter.com/8ihtwLzjs2 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The quarter ended with Philly holding the ball right after. Second Quarter The Eagles punted shortly after teams flipped the field which put the Cowboys offense back up. Given that they were already leading 14-0 this was a chance to really blow things open. Unfortunately they could not and wound up punting the ball for the first time in a while. A big 3rd and 12 conversion from Philadelphia put them within striking distance and while they were unable to fully get home they did give Jake Elliott a chance at a 48-yard field goal. It was good and the visitors had their first points on the day. The Cowboys offense did not miss this time around. KaVontae Turpin was involved again, this time on a jet sweep, and there was a big conversion from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb. But it was Javonte Williams who cased in yet again. This marked his second score on the day and gave Dallas a 21-3 lead. JAVONTE WILLIAMS AGAIN pic.twitter.com/mbe4qovd3I — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The dam finally broke, though. Joe Milton had been showing moments of promise to this point in the game and at long last he delivered. It was a classic Joe Milton throw… meaning it traveled quite a long ways. JOE MILTON'S ARM TALENT IS RIDICULOUS 🎯 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2MLAir7i29 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 The Cowboys received the ball with just over four minutes to go. It felt like an important possession as it would likely be their last one before the half and they received the ball to start the game. Points were essential. In all honesty it was a pretty penalty-filled drive. Officials were calling them left and right, many of them helping the Cowboys, but Dallas was moved back after an apparent touchdown to Brevyn Spann-Ford. On third and goal from the 12-yard line… Dak Prescott found Javonte Williams for a score to close the half. It also marked a hat trick of scores on the day for Williams specifically. JAVONT3 pic.twitter.com/9lMQ1ebII8 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took a knee and it was Miranda Lambert time. Third Quarter Philadelphia went three and out to start the second half which is always great to see. The Cowboys took the field and once again with an opportunity to stretch their lead. Dallas punted it back themselves. This game truly felt over, but obviously with a lot of time left that was not the case in any real way. Football had to be played. Shemar James sacked Joe Milton which helped to ensure the punt streak continued. Philly booted it back and the Cowboys offense returned to the field. It was a little bit of the same for the Cowboys offense in terms of not being able to fully convert. They did score, but only 3 points by way of Brandon Aubrey. This was notable though as it was a 59-yard field goal that he drilled with ease which was great to see given how this season has gone. The FOX broadcast also noted that this was the longest ever field goal made on Thanksgiving all-time. Pretty neat. The third quarter ended right as Philadelphia crossed the 50-yard line… and then Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith again to get another touchdown on the board with 15 seconds left. It was suddenly 31-17, good guys. Fourth Quarter Things did not go particularly well for the Cowboys offense to start the fourth quarter. They faced a fourth and short on their side of the field and left the offense on the field. It was bold, but nobody really thought they were going to run a play. Thankfully they just fished for offsides and punted. Or so we thought. The Cowboys tried to punt… but it was blocked and returned for a Philly touchdown. Out of nowhere it was 31-24 with basically the entire fourth quarter left. EAGLES BLOCKED PUNT TD PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1mrM5lDeTK — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 It goes without saying that the pressure was high. The Cowboys were on the verge of blowing this game. Something had to happen. Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb specifically played like that was the case. They hooked up for a pair of big gains along the drive and then Dak put the exclamation point on things himself by running it on for a touchdown… thanks to some serious hops. DAK!!!! pic.twitter.com/1GdrVEJ8Ls — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 27, 2026 It seemed like this was going to essentially end the game. Have you seen the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, though Philadelphia traveled 42 yards in 3 plays to match the touchdown. Joe Milton literally did by rushing it in himself. Joe Milton takes it in himself! PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ERZiu9S8Kr — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 The Eagles missed the two-point conversion so it was 38-30 Cowboys. In the blink of an eye it was 3rd and 14 right past the team’s own 15-yard line. It appeared as if the Cowboys had pulled off something truly incredible. Dak Prescott found George Pickens for a modest gain, but then he threw a lateral across the field to Hunter Luepke and the fullback took it all the way to the house. He even jumped into the Salvation Army kettle. Unfortunately it was deemed to be a forward pass from Pickens and therefore a penalty which resulted in the loss of the down. Bryan Anger successfully got the punt off this time and the Eagles returned it past midfield. There was still half the fourth quarter remaining. It was then that the Cowboys defense made a play. On third and forever they picked off Joe Milton. Cobie Durant was the hero in question. COBIE DURANT pic.twitter.com/1WmfLgtNqk — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 27, 2026 You would think that this would have given the Cowboys the opportunity to ice the game. You would think that the offense that had been on fire for so long would have scored to fully put things away. They wound up settling for a field goal attempt from 40 yards out. Brandon Aubrey missed. It was unbelievable. Dak's reaction to Aubrey's missed field goal. 📺 FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/PCmN1dFmj9 — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) November 27, 2026 Fine. Mistakes happen. Surely the Cowboys defense would lock in. It took the Eagles just 4 plays to travel 70 yards and score. Seriously. Given the failed two-point conversion earlier though the Eagles had to have one here. They failed again so Dallas retained a slim lead at 38-36. The Cowboys got past midfield. In fact, they got all the way to the Philadelphia 39-yard line. They were facing 4th and 1. Instead of letting Brandon Aubrey try a field goal, he had just missed obviously, the Cowboys chose to go for it. Dak Prescott was sacked. It felt grim. You know what happened. The Eagles pulled off a 60-yard field goal to win 39-38. The Cowboys’ season is over. Unbelievable.

stories.title: Eagles mount furious comeback, beat Cowboys 39-38 in Thanksgiving classic
stories.summary: What looked like a blowout turned into a great one, as Philadelphia stormed back to win in Dallas.
stories.detailText: It was a Thanksgiving Day classic in Dallas. In a wild game that went from an apparent blowout to a thrilling comeback, the Cowboys jumped out to a 31-10 lead and then lost 39-38 when Eagles kicker Jake Elliott hit a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton played by far the best game of his career, throwing for 331 yards, with three touchdown passes and a touchdown run. We've always known Milton had a strong arm, but he showed today that he's more than just a thrower. He can lead an NFL offense as a quarterback. But Dak Prescott is a good quarterback, too, and he turned in a big game of his own. He threw for 291 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. Prescott's favorite receiver was CeeDee Lamb, who finished with 134 receiving yards, and running back Javonte Williams ran for two touchdowns and also caught a touchdown pass. The Eagles, however, got a monster game from wide receiver DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns. Smith was sensational while the Eagles were coming back in the fourth quarter. Special teams miscues killed the Cowboys: The Eagles blocked a punt for a touchdown, and Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Aubrey, who became the highest-paid kicker in the NFL this offseason, is having the worst season of his career. The loss drops the Cowboys to 5-7 and is devastating to their playoff hopes. The 4-7 Eagles aren't contenders, but they played like contenders today.

teamStories.detailText: Typically on Thanksgiving, all eyes in sports are on the football field. That should have especially been true after the Bears pulled out a thrilling 39-35 win over the Detroit Lions on Thursday morning. Yet, all everyone can talk about is Aaron Rodgers and his wild rant on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. Before the Cowboys-Eagles game kicked off on Thursday, the FOX NFL Sunday crew addressed the hot topic in sports. Each member of the pregame show took turns putting Rodgers on blast . Piggybacking off a point made by Michael Strahan, Howie Long dropped the mic. Curt Menefee, left, Terry Bradshaw, Howie Long, Michael Strahan, Jimmy Johnson and Jay Glazer. Cigar Aficionado “If it looks like a duck,” Long said in reference to Rodgers being an awful teammate. Getty Images “If it looks like a duck,” Long said in reference to Rodgers being an awful teammate. “Here’s a guy who has won four MVPs. He won a Super Bowl and as you talked about Michael [Strahan], this is the kind of moment that maybe defines who he is. The Hall of Fame pass rusher then offered a unique opinion that hasn’t been talked about much. The crew reacts to Aaron Rodgers being released by the Steelers. pic.twitter.com/AheBkP7KQl — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) November 26, 2026 “He’s a guy that I think picked the wrong sport. He probably should have played tennis. It’s an individual sport.” The conversation surrounding the enigmatic QB and whether or not he is a good teammate has raged for years. He would go on to talk about how every player who has ever suited up in the NFL has had problems. Problems with coaches, teammates, team personnel, etc. But there is a way in which it should be handled. For most of Rodgers’ career, he vilified players who talked about team issues publicly. all everyone can talk about is Aaron Rodgers and his wild rant on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. AP Photo/Chris Szagola Then he went scorched earth after learning he was benched by Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. Former Steelers quarterback and four-time Super Bowl winner Terry Bradshaw had arguably the strongest words, wishing Rodgers would disappear never to be seen again. “I’m sorry Aaron Rodgers had to do this. I’m sorry he had to go public with all of this. Am I surprised? Absolutely not. But one thing from Rodgers’ wild rant stood out. “One thing he said, he said ‘when I’m through playing here in Pittsburgh, I’ll disappear and you’ll never hear or see of me again.’ “I hope this is one time he is telling the truth.” Wow! Tell us how you really feel, Terry. teamStories.summary: Brock Bowers was back at practice again, but with a heavy twist.
teamStories.detailText: Brock Bowers practiced on a limited basis for the second straight day Thursday, with one caveat for anyone encouraged by the sight of the Raiders tight end back on the field. The ankle that kept him out of last week’s game in Denver was heavily wrapped. Whether that was a precaution or a sign the ankle still has a ways to go remains to be seen. At this point, Bowers’ availability for Sunday night’s game against the Browns in Cleveland appears headed toward a game-day decision. Brock Bowers comes out for Thanksgiving Day practice with his right ankle prepped by the trainers. His status for Sunday is still unknown. pic.twitter.com/j5mHp79AM1 — Kevin Bolinger (@KevinFOX5Vegas) November 26, 2026 Either way, there’s someone in Cleveland who’d love to see him. You get the idea Browns coach Todd Monken would just prefer their reunion take place during pregame warmups, with Bowers in street clothes. Monken was Georgia’s offensive coordinator when he and Bowers won back-to-back national championships . He spent those two seasons dreaming up ways to get Bowers the ball. Given a week to figure out how to keep it away from him, Monken fondly recalled what he was up against. At Georgia, they had a name for the kid who would chase down every ball you threw him, bring it back and look at you like he couldn’t think of a reason you’d stop throwing it. Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders looks on prior to a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images Buddy the Yellow Lab. “You could play ball all day and his tongue would be hanging out, and he never wanted to come out, man,” Monken told reporters this week. “He would just want to keep playing.” As for the prospect of seeing his old tight end Sunday, Monken allowed himself a little wishful thinking. “And I would tell anybody that listened to him, I said, this guy’s just different, you know,” Monken said. “And hopefully he’s still hurt.” Monken was kidding. We think, anyway. Good luck selling Buddy on another Sunday off. “We all really want to play,” Bowers said. “It’s really hard mentally on me to miss time.” Imagine how Fernando Mendoza feels. The rookie quarterback makes his third NFL start Sunday and has barely had a chance to find out what life is like with Bowers. They connected twice for 18 yards on the opening series against Seattle in Mendoza’s debut. Bowers hurt his ankle on that drive. That’s the extent of their work together on game day. Brock Bowers, left, and Fernando Mendoza of the Las Vegas Raiders wait to be introduced before playing the Seattle Seahawks, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Las Vegas. Getty Images Consider what Mendoza stands to get back. Bowers caught 112 passes for 1,194 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie, then added 64 catches for 680 yards and seven scores in 12 games last year. In eight appearances this season, he has 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns. That’s 226 catches, 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games. Thirty-five of his 50 catches this year have moved the chains. For a young quarterback trying to get the ball out before the rush gets home, there’s considerable appeal in throwing a five-yard pass to a guy who can get you 10. Georgia’s coaches got their first look at that extra gear before anyone threw Bowers a pass. The COVID-19 shutdown had cost the kid from Napa, California, his entire senior football season. On the first day of winter conditioning in Athens, all the freshman had to do was finish a timed run with the other tight ends. “He’s like 10 yards in front of all of them,” Monken said. Monken figures he’d have stayed with the pack his first day, lest an older teammate get the idea the new guy was showing off. Georgia tight ends coach Todd Hartley remembers what happened when they lined up again. Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken watches the third quarter against the Houston Texans on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “This dude was winning every sprint,” Hartley said. “The fastest dude out there, the hardest worker. And we’re like, ‘Oh, my God.’ I mean, we knew he was fast, but we didn’t know he was fast-fast, or had a work ethic like this.” Before Bowers won either of his two Mackey Awards as the nation’s best tight end, he had changed what a day’s work looked like in Athens. The guys trying to beat him out could do the math. “Brock Bowers was the best thing to happen to us. Not just because he had a million catches and won two Mackey Awards. But because he set a standard for work,” Hartley said. “And from the very beginning, [other players] saw that kid and said, ‘If I’m going to see the field, I got to step my game up.’” Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders leaves the field after being injured during a game against the Seattle Seahawks in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images Long before Georgia, Bowers and his dad had their own Sunday night game. With football on TV, Bowers drew a line in the carpet for a sideline. His dad threw him a Nerf football, and Bowers tried to come down with his feet in. All these years later, somebody else still has to tell him when it’s time to quit. “I’m always pushing to play no matter what,” Bowers said. Monken could have told the Raiders that much.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images Considering the team’s defense ranks dead last in points allowed and yielding the second-worst amount of yards allowed, the Las Vegas Raiders special teams can ill affording adding to the overall woes. Field position comes at a premium in the NFL and for the Silver & Black, a disadvantage of that nature puts Rob Leonard’s defense in dire straits. Which makes the pair of times Raiders punter AJ Cole III’s boots were blocked by the Denver Broncos in the Week 11 38-24 loss a cause for concern. “I have to watch the tape,” Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said when asked about the punt protection in the postgame press conference. “Two punts were huge. They were big,” Denver head coach Sean Payton said after the game. “One of them I know was a rush. When you look at what that does field position-wise and just say it’s a 40-yard swing, it’s almost like a turnover.” Even a day later, when the NFL statisticians officially marked the two punts as deflected and not blocked — due to the ball crossing the line of scrimmage — a sour taste remains in the Raiders special teams room. The first deflection occurred in the opening quarter when Denver’s Sai’Vion Jones bull rushed up the middle and changed the trajectory of Cole’s boot with his forearm. The ball eventually settled two yards past the line of scrimmage. The second occurred a quarter later with Dondrea Tillman tipping Cole’s punt limiting the boot to just 27 yards. It was indeed a forgettable Mile High outing for not only Cole, but special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis. BLOCKED‼️ 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/9WKuW8iZYF — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 22, 2026 Shoring up the blocking and protection assignments on punts is a must as the Raiders’ Week 12 matchup with the Cleveland Browns was flexed to the Sunday night primetime slot instead of the standard afternoon affair it was originally was. Everything gets amplified under the lights in front of a national audience and repeating the lack of protection which resulted in Cole’s normally booming punts ricocheting off a defender’s appendage isn’t ideal. Where They Stand With 40 punts on the season, Cole is ranked 12th amongst his punting brethren in the league. The 2,029 yards his kicking foot has amassed ranks ninth while his 50.7 yards per punt average is third-best in the NFL. Cole’s 43.8 net yards per punt — average that subtracts return and touchback yards — is seventh-best as the league average on average yards per boot and net yards per punt are 47.7 and 42.2, respectively. The 31-year-old punter has four touchbacks which puts him at fifth-most and with 15 of his boots landing inside or being downed in the opponent’s 20-yard line puts him right in the middle at 16th overall. That’s the area where Cole is under the league average of 39.9 percent of kicks pinning opponents deep with his being 37.5 percent. In comparison, the Philadelphia Eagles’ Braden Mann leads the league in punts (53) and yardage (2,566) and he also owns the longest boot of the season with an 86-yard blast. The New York Giants’ Jordan Stout tops the yards per punt average at 51.7 — the Kansas City Chiefs’ Matt Araiza is second at 51.0 — while the G-Men’s boot specialist is atop the league with a 44.7 net yards average per boot. Mann also leads the NFL with 24 of his 53 punts pinning opponents within their own 20-yard line. Place kicking-wise, Matt Gay has certainly rekindled the accurate and dependable ways with DeCamillis in Las Vegas, much like the duo had during their respective time with the Los Angeles Rams. Matt Gay's two best seasons arrived in 2021 and 2022 with Joe DeCamillis as special teams boss with the Rams. Trying to recapture those 2 years where Gay was 94.1 and 93.3 percent in field goals (32-of-34 & 28-of-30). #Raiders #RaiderNation https://t.co/usCH2a5EKS — Ray Aspuria (@AsukalAspuria) March 10, 2026 As noted in the tweet above, Gay’s two best seasons in his eight seasons in the NFL were with DeCamillis in Los Angeles. The initial skepticism of Gay being a productive replacement for long time kicker Daniel Carlson have been certainly allayed. At 22-of-24 on field goals this season, the 32-year-old kicker has the sixth-best accuracy percentage at 91.7 percent. Gay’s long of 59 yards gives him the sixth-longest boot amongst his contemporaries and going 25-for-25 on extra points gives him the third-best percentage in that department. Gay’s misses this season were from 49 yards and 51 yards out — both in the month of October. The first occurred in Week 5 against the New England Patriots (Gay finish 1-for-2 on field goals that game) and the second a Week 7 miss against the Rams (he finished 3-for-4 that day). With the 22 field goals and 25 extra points made so far during the Raiders’ 2026 campaign, Gay (unsurprisingly) leads the team in points scored at 91. For comparison’s sake, there’s only one kicker who hasn’t missed a field goal attempt this season: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ Chase McLaughlin who is 22-for-22. A total of 12 kickers are perfect on extra points heading into Week 12 action. The NFL average for field goal percentage is 84.7 percent while it’s 95.5 percent on extra points. Return game-wise, Las Vegas boasts one of the top kick returners in running back Dylan Laube. Raiders RB Dylan Laube is the first player in the NFL this season to return a kickoff for a touchdown. pic.twitter.com/nhu44RpO5j — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 1, 2026 The 27-year-old reserve tailback is one of two return men in the league to house a kickoff. The 95-yard burst Laube had against the New York Jets in the Raiders’ Week 8 38-33 victory was the first end zone visit on a kick return this season. Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Devontez Walker housed a kickoff (86-yard gallop) in Week 11. Laube currently ranks second in average yards per return at 29.9. He trails Buffalo Bills running back Ray Davis (30.1 average) in that department. In terms of total kick return yards, Laube is third at a tally of 956. Tennessee Titans wideout Chimere Dike and Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Dohnte Meyers are ahead at 1,112 and 968 yards, respectively. The Raiders punt return game hasn’t been as explosive. Rookie wide receiver Malik Benson has seven returns for 94 yards while veteran wideout Deven Thompkins has one for 18 yards and Laube has two for 13 yards. Las Vegas is more apt to signal fair catch than return punts.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stop me if you’ve heard this before, but the Las Vegas Raiders defense has got a lot of growing to do to catch up with the offense. They have come within one score of, or surpassed, the 40-point threshold for the sixth time in 11 games. Pointing fingers Head coach Klint Kubiak said they win as a team and lose as a team; refusing to point fingers is noble and expected of the head coach. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard elected not to take the high road, instead making a snide comment: “Fatigue makes cowards of us all…when you’re on the field a long time, mistakes tend to happen more often.” But here, we aren’t limited by nobility; Leonard would have gotten a pass until he decided to open his mouth and speak on an offense ranking 29 th in time of possession but 6 th in total points. So let us start by looking at who has been truly responsible for this lackluster defense. Leonard is the one calling the defensive plays and maintaining a league-worst defensive efficiency allowed, a paltry 48.1% defensive success rate and a 15.9% explosive play rate. No rush at all No one is doing jack up front for the Raiders defensive line outside of Maxx Crosby. Over the last three weeks, the Raiders defensive line has 2.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, seven quarterback hits, 1 forced fumble and two pass breakups. Crosby is the owner of every single one of those stats except one quarterback hit from Kwity Paye, Malcolm Koonce and Tonka Hemingway, along with the 0.5 sack, forced fumble and two pass breakups that Folorunso Fatukasi has produced. Kwity Paye , a high-priced free agent acquisition, hasn’t had a sack since Week 6 at home against the Buffalo Bills. Coincidentally, that happened to be the date of his last tackle for loss as well. His last quarterback hit was against Brock Purdy in Week 9. Hardly worthy of his lofty three-year, $48 million ($16 million average) contract. Cutting him with a June-1 designation saves roughly $6.01 million, with $16.824 million (one year’s salary) dead cap. At the rate of one sack every 5-6 weeks, one quarterback hit roughly every 2-3 weeks and a tackle for loss every six weeks, the rubber is going to have to meet the road at some point. Malcolm Koonce, last year Koonce got a pass for coming off an injured knee and was kept over a more deserving K’Lavon Chaisson. After receiving a good-faith one-year $11.01 million contract, his good start to the 2026 season has faded into oblivion along with his productivity. Over the last three games, he has two tackles and a quarterback hit. This season, he has accounted for 12 tackles, seven quarterback hits, three sacks, two forced fumbles and 1 tackle for loss. His last 0.5 sack was in Week 5 against the New England Patriots; the quarterback hit against the Denver Broncos on Sunday was his first impact as a rusher in six weeks. Adam Butler , according to Pro Football Focus, ranks 84 th out of 134 qualified interior defensive linemen. Strangely enough, Butler’s best grade is as a run defender, ranking 49 th of 134 and then comes the fall. His 21 total tackles are outside the Top 50 defensive tackles; his 0.5 sacks are outside the Top 75 defensive tackles; his seven total quarterback pressures are in the bottom third of qualifying defensive interiors. Defensive backfield Eric Stokes has played so poorly as of late that it is baffling how he is still starting. At this point, he has been every opponent’s favorite target; more so than even the rookies. When he isn’t giving up on plays, he is getting beaten like a drum. Stokes is allowing a passer rating of 115.2, making him the 9th-worst cover corner in the league coming out of week 10. What’s worse is that number has been steadily climbing over the last three weeks. In weeks 8-10, he posted a passer rating of 116.1. Additionally, when it comes to penalties, he has four accepted pass interference calls resulting in 58 yards; the first being tied for 5th most and the latter being the 5th most in the league. Stokes may have five pass breakups this season, but he still hasn’t recorded an interception since week 4 of his rookie season. Hezekiah Masses, Jermod McCoy, Darien Porter: All three are rookie cornerbacks who must be afforded an opportunity to learn their craft and experience bumps and bruises along the way. Before blaming them for all the explosive plays generated, we have to understand they are being asked to cover for a league-worst 3.0 seconds to throw and 4 th -worst in pocket time allowed, 2.72 seconds. Individually, they have all experienced success in one way, shape, or form. All of these young defensive backs need to get in the weight room and transform their bodies from college to the pros. Getting acclimated to the league is a process and all of these young players have shown promise. Masses has three interceptions this year but is still searching for a permanent positional home. Slightly undersized, he has the heart of a lion but needs a good NFL strength and development plan in the offseason. Out wide, he has three interceptions, but his productivity in the slot has been an improvement over veteran Taron Johnson, which offers positional versatility. He is a better man-coverage corner than soft zone but can do both. A ferocious blitzer who can get home when activated but is still too small to be a nickel linebacker. One of the few blemishes has been his ability to hold contain when he’s the last defender on the line. Porter the second-year cornerback, is a bit of an enigma. Unable to keep his starting job locked down from Masses and McCoy, he hasn’t been bad and has proven that, if utilized correctly, he can be an asset to the defense. Porter is a converted wide receiver with size, speed and length who specializes in press-man coverage. However, the main issue is the press-bail and zone technique he is being asked to play is a style which isn’t conducive to what he does best. He is a good and willing tackler, better suited to larger, less quick-twitch receivers. Opposite of Stokes, he is the second-best tackler out past the edges. McCoy , when healthy, has the tools to be the best of the bunch. Watching him stay balanced, controlled and locate the football was a sight for sore eyes. Playing the ball all the way through the catching process and being able to punch the ball out is what the Raiders need. Tackling in the run game was a problem against the Broncos. All in all, for a rookie making his second start, there are some encouraging signs but also plenty of room for improvement. Defending the run Enough can’t be said about how disappointing the run defense has been. This season, the 16 rushing touchdowns allowed are tied for the most in the league. The Raiders are allowing 149.5 yards per game, ranking 31st, and 4.82 yards per carry, ranking 30th in the league. Surprisingly, the 51 missed tackles are middle of the pack, so the reality is they are getting outmuscled. Against the Broncos, the Raiders lost three defensive tackles to injury. Whether they are able to play in the Sunday Night Game against the Cleveland Browns remains to be seen. If they are not, the run defense stands to be even worse.

teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders play at the Cleveland Browns on Sunday night. Kickoff is at 5:20 p.m. PT. Here are three things to know about the Browns: Coach is doing work: When the Browns hired longtime NFL assistant Todd Monken as their head coach this offseason it really didn’t move the radar. It wasn’t considered a sexy pick. But the no -nonsense offensive minded job has his team playing well at 6-4. He seems to be a fit for the city and for team franchise. The first-time NFL head coach, 60, is a dark horse NFL Coach of the Year candidate Playoff history: The Browns known for being a woebegone franchise that has never been to a Super Bowl. But there are looking to go to the payoffs for the third time this decade. Nothing much was expected from this team, but they are winning more than they are losing. Tough at home and in the fourth quarter: The Browns have had six fourth-quarterback comebacks and they are a perfect 4-0 at home. Do you think the Dawg Pound will be fired up for their first Sunday Night Football game in five years? Defense can be run on: The Browns’ defense is solid, but it can give up big plays on the ground. They have allowed 34 run plays of 10 plus yards this season. The Raiders have struggled against the run for much of this season, but there is an opportunity for some chunk plays.
